name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

When matching a layer norm pattern, the operand of the reduction that calculates
the expectation may differ from the layer norm input by a reshape or bitcast
that adds or removes degenerate dimensions. `MatchLayerNorm` nevertheless used
the dimensions of the reduction to index into the shape of the input when
deriving the transpose order and the shape of the cuDNN operands. If the
reduction's operand had a higher rank than the input, this resulted in
out-of-bounds accesses of the inverse transpose order and of the input's
dimensions.

The rewrite is now skipped unless all reduction dimensions are valid dimensions
of the input and select the same non-degenerate dimensions in the input as in
the reduction's operand. Patterns for which the dimensions agree are still
rewritten.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

`CpuInstructionFusion` has no bound on how large a loop fusion may grow. The only size-related guard, `FusionNodeIndexingEvaluation::CodeDuplicationTooHigh`, is skipped entirely when the pass runs with `may_duplicate=false`, which `cpu_compiler.cc` selects whenever `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` is set.

On reverse-mode AD programs of stencil codes (Enzyme-MLIR / Reactant differentiating the Oceananigans ocean model) this produces loop fusions with 210–250 operands and 880–1045 fused instructions per output element: the `pad`-accumulate chain of every halo'd adjoint pulls in each stencil tap's whole producer DAG. The elemental emitter's per-element code for such a fusion neither vectorizes nor fits in registers; the reverse loop ran ~10× the primal while doing 4.2× its FLOPs.

This change adds an operand budget, checked independently of `may_duplicate()`: a producer is not fused into an existing fusion if the result would have more than `xla_cpu_max_fusion_operands` distinct operands (default 96, matching the GPU backend's `MaxOperandsAndOutputsPerFusion`). The option is an `xla_backend_extra_options` entry read through `cpu_options`; a value `<= 0` disables the check.

The budget is deliberately on operands only. An earlier revision also capped the number of fused instructions (512), which split long single-input elementwise chains and changed numerics in two JAX CPU tests: (a) `jax.scipy.special.iv` (f32) is a 540-instruction chain using double-float arithmetic; XLA:CPU sets `contract` on all FP arithmetic, so a kernel boundary prevents FMA contraction across it and breaks the error-free transformations (1.36 ULP instead of ≤ 1). (b) `ndtri_exp` gradient (bf16) differs on subnormal inputs: XLA:CPU runs kernels with denormals-are-zero, but LLVM folds `y == 0` on a bf16→f32 convert into an integer test on the bits, while `y < 0` stays a `ucomiss` that honors DAZ; which fold applies depends on the kernel boundaries. Both effects are pre-existing properties of XLA:CPU that any change in fusion boundaries can expose; the operand cap alone does not split these chains (they have 1–13 operands) and does not change either test.

Measurements (Oceananigans channel-model gradient, 8 time steps, one x86 core, `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` on; min / median of 3 calls):

| operand cap | gradient | primal |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched | 28.1 / 28.9 s | 3.01 s |
| disabled (`0`, control) | 28.0 / 29.3 s | — |
| 128 | 17.4 / 17.7 s | — |
| 96 (default) | 13.8 / 14.2 s | 2.89 s |
| 64 | 14.8 / 14.9 s | — |
| 48 | 11.7–13.1 / 12.2–13.2 s | 2.37 s |
| 32 | 12.8 / 13.1 s | 2.19 s |

(The 48 row spans four runs with the earlier instruction cap at 512, 1024, 4096 and disabled: 13.0, 11.7, 12.8, 13.1 s min — the instruction cap had no measurable effect, which is why it was dropped.) Results are bit-identical in the objective and agree with the unpatched build to rel. L2 ≤ 2e-15 in every gradient field.

The default is 96 rather than 48 based on a sweep over a suite of 80 CPU benchmark HLO models (A/B against head, 20 runs each). Compiling every model at several caps shows that any cap from 48 to 128 changes the fused HLO of the same two models (every other model has at most 42 operands per fusion), whereas the TORAX plasma-simulation models have fusions of 49–267 operands and are sensitive to the exact value: at cap 48 three of them regress 2–5% in wall time on Granite Rapids (4–13% on AMD Rome), while at cap 96 none regresses by more than 1% and their geomean improves by 1.2% (Granite Rapids) / 2.6% (Rome). The two models affected at any cap are within ±2% at either value. Suite-wide, the cap leaves runtime unchanged (geomean −0.2%) and improves compile wall time by 2% at the cost of 2% more compile CPU time.

Tests: `cpu_instruction_fusion_test` gains five cases on a 120-tap pad/add chain: the default budget splits it (largest fusion exactly 96 operands), also with `may_duplicate=false`, the budget is configurable (16), disabling it fuses the whole chain into one fusion, and a malformed option value is rejected with `InvalidArgument`.

The same change is vendored as a patch in Enzyme-JAX (https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3882, https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3883).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

Dataflow analysis crashes on a late bound `async-start` wrapping `dynamic-update-slice`. Such a start has no operands; its operands and output are bound on the `async-update`. `UpdateAsyncStartValueSet` special cased DUS starts and read `operand(0)` without checking that it exists.

The DUS case moves into `UpdateAsyncChainOutputValueSet`. A DUS start still forwards its destination operand to `{1}`, but only when the start has that operand; otherwise it falls back to the wrapped root and the existing bound checks skip the unbound output. The forwarding is required: without it, a loop carried DUS start feeds the wrapped result back into the shared destination parameter, which then has two values and fails in place aliasing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix sub-byte operand read bytes and batched dot shared-memory sizing.

Fusion operand read estimation previously rounded each element up to whole
bytes, overcounting tiled read bytes and L2 read traffic by 2x on bit-packed
4-bit quantized operands (assuming sub-byte operands are packed in memory).
Meanwhile, per-block dot shared-memory sizing omitted the batch tile multiplier
(`b > 1`), truncated odd bit totals via floor division by 8, and sized `pred`
tiles at 1 bit instead of 8-bit storage width.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

head_commit.message:
Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` passed the shape indices of an
`OriginalValueProto` to `OriginalValue::FromProto` without checking them
against the shape of the instruction. The tuple tree built from these indices
grows with the magnitude and the length of the indices, so a small malformed
proto could cause excessive memory allocation or very deep recursion before
the HLO verifier had a chance to run.

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` now returns an `InvalidArgument` error if an
element of the original value has a shape index that does not exist in the
shape of the instruction, which bounds the size of the tree by the size of the
shape. The HLO verifier already rejects original values whose tuple structure
differs from the instruction shape, so modules that pass verification are not
affected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020100033

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:LHS] Fix out-of-bounds access when no annotated node can be scheduled

head_commit.message:
[XLA:LHS] Fix out-of-bounds access when no annotated node can be scheduled

`FindAndExtractBestAnnotatedNode` removed the chosen node from the annotation
ready set by swapping it with the last element, without checking that a node
had been chosen. When every ready node of the annotation group crosses the
resource overlap limit, the iterator still points past the end of the vector,
so the swap read and wrote one element out of bounds before the caller reported
the failure.

Return early in that case and leave the ready set untouched. The caller already
turns the missing node into an error status, so scheduling such a module now
fails cleanly instead of corrupting memory.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

`ShapeVerifier::HandleSort` only checked that the sort dimension is smaller
than the operand rank. Because the comparison is signed, a negative sort
dimension in an HLO module (for example one deserialized from a proto or
parsed from HLO text) passed verification. Passes and backend code
generation that run afterwards index operand shapes with the sort dimension
without further checks, which leads to out-of-bounds accesses.

The verifier now also requires the sort dimension to be non-negative, so
such modules are rejected with an error before any pass consumes them.

The error message now reports the rank of the first operand instead of
reading the dimensions of the sort result shape, which is a tuple for
sorts with more than one operand and cannot be queried for dimensions.

display_title: [ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

 - RcclCommunicator had no LaunchReduce; CollectiveReduce runtime support
   was added for NCCL only. Implemented on top of ncclReduce.
 - Backend::CreateGpuAllocators registered no collective memory space
   allocator, so any module whose device count equals the visible device
   count died with "No allocator found ... memory space 7" once buffer
   assignment colored its temp buffer S(7). Not ROCm specific.
 - MORI dlopen()s amd_smi by unversioned name and exit(-1)s when that
   fails, which no hermetic ROCm build can satisfy; XLA now hands it the
   path of the copy already mapped into the process.
 - ShardedAutotuningWorks hard-coded TCP port 12345 and failed when an
   unrelated process held it; it now picks a free port.
 - Symmetric-memory ragged-all-to-all needs a
   NCCL LSA window; it is CUDA-only and has no RCCL equivalent.
 - Command-buffer control flow and cross-host
   disabled on ROCm by CommandBufferConversionPass and IsLsaPossible().

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Bound the traversal of MLIR locations when exporting them to HLO metadata.

head_commit.message:
Bound the traversal of MLIR locations when exporting them to HLO metadata.

MLIR uniques locations, so nested locations (`CallSiteLoc`, `FusedLoc`,
`NameLoc`) can share sub-locations and form a DAG. The MHLO to HLO export
walked such locations recursively as trees when building op names, stack frames,
and source file/line metadata. With shared sub-locations, the work and the size
of the exported metadata grew exponentially with the nesting depth, and deeply
nested locations could overflow the C++ call stack.

Convert these traversals to iterative worklists, visit at most 4096 locations
per exported location, and cap the exported `op_name` at 4096 bytes by dropping
the names that do not fit. Locations emitted by frontends are far smaller, so
their metadata is unchanged; only pathologically nested or oversized locations
get truncated metadata. Empty names are now skipped instead of adding a
separator to the `op_name`.

Shared sub-locations are still visited every time they occur instead of being
deduplicated, because repeated locations are legitimate, for example the stack
frames of a recursive function.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

head_commit.message:
[XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

📝 Summary of Changes

HostOffloader::WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths follows the offloaded buffer through its users. For a generic user it keeps the same shape index, so a send user is tracked as the whole send result tuple, its send-done user is tracked as a token, and if that token is returned from the entry computation the pass ends up in the output streaming check, which does CHECK(leaf.has_layout()) on the entry result leaves. Tokens never have a layout, so the compiler aborts.

A token carries no data, so an offloaded buffer never flows through it (send-done only produces a token; the data stays in send's output {0}). This change skips token-shaped successors in the walk, and makes the output streaming check skip non-array leaves (the send result tuple itself has a token leaf, so returning the send from the entry computation hit the same CHECK). Arrays and tuples are handled exactly as before, and the existing send test (BasicHostTransferSendNoCrash) still gets its copy to host memory in front of the send.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50971. The module from the issue (MoveToHost -> send -> send-done -> ROOT tuple(send-done)) aborts GPU compilation at HEAD with "Check failed: leaf.has_layout() Expecting output shape of entry computation to have a layout." With this change it gets the same clean error as the module without the MoveToHost ("Expected recv to match send", the fuzzer module has no matching recv), and a properly paired program compiles normally.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in xla/hlo/transforms/host_offloader_test.cc. SendDoneTokenReturnedFromEntryNoCrash runs the pass on the issue's module and checks that it succeeds, that the root is still tuple(send-done(send(copy(param), after-all))), that the copy is in host memory and the parameter is not, and that no annotations remain. SendResultReturnedFromEntryNoCrash returns the send itself from the entry computation and expects a clean error (the offloaded data would be returned in a device memory output). Without the source change both tests abort with the CHECK from the issue.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added. Checked manually with run_hlo_module

display_title: PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

head_commit.message:
PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52161

ROCm only change, This is to help us get stable address which we can use to avoid collective recapture whenever stable address is there.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

On ROCm, `--xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color` gets a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for memory space `kTempBuffer`. Next to a preallocated default pool it may use the device memory that the default pool's memory fraction leaves, like the collective pool. without preallocation it has the default pool's limit.

## 🎯 Justification

The flag assigns temp buffers to `kTempBuffer`, but only CUDA registered an allocator for that space. On ROCm, an executable whose temp allocations are combined fails:

```
INTERNAL: No allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter for device ordinal 0 and memory space 2
```

Only temp buffers use the new pool, so each execution gets the same temp address, which is what the flag is for.

- Like CUDA's pool, it sits outside the default pool: with a preallocated default pool, temp buffers must fit in what the default pool's memory fraction leaves, so a large temp buffer can run out of memory with the flag on and fit with it off. Lowering the memory fraction makes room, a fraction that leaves nothing is rejected when the client is created.
- Unlike CUDA's pool (sync mode), it does not synchronize the stream on allocate or free.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix · 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`:
- `TempBufferColorUsesSeparatePool`: a `kTempBuffer` allocation leaves the default pool untouched and gets its address back after an intervening default allocation.
- `TempBufferColorKeepsTempAddressStable`: runs an HLO whose temp allocation is recoloured; checks the results and that the temp address stays the same over three executions.

Both fail without this change with the error above.

`gpu_helpers_test` (`BfcMemorySizingTest`):
- `TempBufferPoolGetsWhatAPreallocatedPoolLeaves`: next to a default pool preallocated at 0.75 of device memory, the temp pool's limit is the remaining quarter.
- `TempBufferPoolHasDefaultLimitWithoutPreallocation`: without preallocation the temp pool keeps the default pool's limit.
- `TempBufferPoolNeedsMemoryLeftByPreallocatedPool`: a fraction of 1.0 is rejected.

`allocator_config_test`: `MemFractionTest.LeftIsWhatTheStartFractionLeaves`.

These targets pass on MI355X (ROCm 10.2); `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test` and `gpu_helpers_test` also pass on B300 (CUDA 13).

## 🧪 Execution Tests

JAX on MI355X, ROCm 10.0, with the flag on 1 GPU and on 2 GPUs with an all-reduce: results are identical to the flag off under `--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true`.

Copybara import of the project:

--

[ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

- The flag puts temp buffers in memory space kTempBuffer, but only CUDA
  registered an allocator for it. On ROCm, execution failed with "No
  allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter ... memory space 2".
- On ROCm, register a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for

  they keep the same address across executions.
- Next to a preallocated default pool, the temp pool gets the device
  memory that the default pool's start fraction leaves, like the
  collective pool; MemFractionLeft computes that remainder for both.
  Without preallocation it keeps the default pool's limit. Creating the
  client fails with a clear error if nothing is left for the temp pool.
- CreateBFCAllocator takes a name prefix (default "GPU", so existing
  pools keep GPU_<n>_bfc).
- In SharedPoolAnchorsCollectiveMemoryAtLowerEnd, convert device
  addresses to uintptr_t with reinterpret_cast instead of
  absl::bit_cast. The clang 18 static analyzer crashes comparing
  bit_cast pointer values, which fails clang-tidy on any change to

- Update the flag's help text and add tests.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add CuDnnGemmDimensions to compute the dimensions of cuDNN GEMM fusions with ShapeTracker.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add CuDnnGemmDimensions to compute the dimensions of cuDNN GEMM fusions with ShapeTracker.

`CuDnnFusionCompiler` derives the sizes and strides of the tensors of dot /
scaled-dot cuDNN fusions with `TritonFusionAnalysis`, which is part of the
legacy Triton GEMM tiling infrastructure that we want to remove: it no longer
tiles or emits fusions and does not support many of today's fusions.

`CuDnnGemmDimensions` replaces it in a follow-up change (cl/1018233906), using these steps:

1.  Use ShapeTracker to relate every instruction to one 'port' of the dot (lhs, rhs, output).
2.  Check cuDNN restrictions (i.e. non-scalar instructions must relate to the dot in a single way, because the cuDNN graph has a single tensor per instruction - for example, `dot(p, p)` and `d + transpose(d)` are rejected).
3.  Use ShapeTracker to record sizes and strides of each operand and output. This translates all bitcasts/transposes that are allowed into sizes and strides for cuDNN to read the correct tensor for operand (e.g. [batch, M, K] for lhs).

I haven't replaced TritonFusionAnalysis immediately because I still need to support strides and split-M, which happen in follow up CLs.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017387793

display_title: [ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

 - RcclCommunicator had no LaunchReduce; CollectiveReduce runtime support
   was added for NCCL only. Implemented on top of ncclReduce.
 - Backend::CreateGpuAllocators registered no collective memory space
   allocator, so any module whose device count equals the visible device
   count died with "No allocator found ... memory space 7" once buffer
   assignment colored its temp buffer S(7). Not ROCm specific.
 - MORI dlopen()s amd_smi by unversioned name and exit(-1)s when that
   fails, which no hermetic ROCm build can satisfy; XLA now hands it the
   path of the copy already mapped into the process.
 - ShardedAutotuningWorks hard-coded TCP port 12345 and failed when an
   unrelated process held it; it now picks a free port.
 - Symmetric-memory ragged-all-to-all needs a
   NCCL LSA window; it is CUDA-only and has no RCCL equivalent.
 - Command-buffer control flow and cross-host
   disabled on ROCm by CommandBufferConversionPass and IsLsaPossible().

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

Slices are tracked alongside the ShapeTracker as per-dimension ranges of the
port of the dot: the ShapeTracker describes the unsliced tensor, and the ranges
become the `slices` of the cuDNN tensor. Nested slices are combined.

A slice can be followed by shape transformations before it reaches the dot,
e.g. `dot(transpose(slice(p)), ...)`. When a slice is reached, it is moved to
the port side of the ShapeTracker: the steps of the ShapeTracker are replayed
on the shape of the operand of the slice, carrying the sliced range of every
dimension along. Transposes permute the ranges. Reshapes can merge or split a
sliced dimension as long as the slice remains a range of a single dimension:
only the major-most dimension of a group of merged dimensions can be sliced,
and the range has to be aligned to the dimensions that it is split into.

A sliced dimension has to be a whole canonical dimension of the cuDNN tensor.
Strided slices are rejected. Slices of operands after the dot are rejected as
well: cuDNN builds plans for such graphs but fails to execute them
(CUDNN_STATUS_BAD_PARAM_NULL_POINTER).
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017387797

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Work around large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Retry large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

WSL can reject large POSIX-FD VMM allocations with OUT_OF_MEMORY despite
sufficient free memory. Try the full-size allocation first, then retry
with backing chunks of at most 1 GiB on WSL with fabric handles disabled
and multicast unsupported. Exclude locality-domain allocations and map the
chunks into one contiguous virtual address range.

Keep POSIX-FD exportability to preserve multi-GPU support under WSL2.
Disabling enable_posix_fd_handle would be shorter, but removes handles
needed by cross-process GPU sharing and some NCCL paths.

Retain only the original first handle and release later creation
references after mapping. Track the mapped prefix for rollback and keep
the existing deallocation path.

Add a manual 6 GiB plus padding allocator regression and a WSL-only NCCL
regression that registers independent 6 GiB buffers, transfers the full
buffer, and checks both sides of each 1 GiB boundary. Skip the NCCL test
before GPU discovery on other operating systems and retain hardware,
memory, and chunking checks.

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight non-RDMA allocator tests, the manual
6 GiB regression, clang-format 17.0.6, and git diff --check pass. Three
upstream locality tests skip for version or hardware requirements. The
full two-GPU NCCL test skips on this single-GPU machine. Earlier local
two-process probes transferred a 6 GiB chunked source into an independent
256 MiB receiver; write and forced peer-read paths passed. The read probe
refreshed source registration per window and confirmed two-segment
imports at all five boundaries. Distinct-GPU execution remains untested.

display_title: Hoist stride-1 minor dimension out of BroadcastHelper inner loop in literal.cc.

head_commit.message:
Hoist stride-1 minor dimension out of BroadcastHelper inner loop in literal.cc.

BroadcastHelper previously invoked IndexUtil::MultidimensionalIndexToLinearIndex
and IndexUtil::BumpIndices on every output element, even along the contiguous
stride-1 most-minor layout dimension. Hoist result_minor_to_major[0] out of
broadcast_shape and fill inner_broadcast_size contiguous elements directly (via
memset for 1-byte elements and a contiguous memcpy loop otherwise), yielding a
1.52x geomean speedup across literal broadcast/populate benchmarks (14.24x on
BM_BroadcastVectorToMatrix/16/1024).

Changes:
- Add a concise `build_tools/ci/bep_annotations.py` (and `bep_annotations_test.py`) to parse failed/final-failed `testResult`, failed `action`, and `aborted` BEP events (skipping flaky tests that ultimately passed), extract the invocation ID / `--bes_results_url` link, and emit up to 10 bounded (`<= 3500` escaped chars) `::error` workflow commands per step with up to the last 50 lines of `test.log` / `stderr`. - Add best-effort (`continue-on-error: true`, `if: failure() || cancelled()`) annotation steps to `.github/workflows/rocm_ci.yml` for both the JAX and XLA jobs.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

head_commit.message:
Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` passed the shape indices of an
`OriginalValueProto` to `OriginalValue::FromProto` without checking them
against the shape of the instruction. The tuple tree built from these indices
grows with the magnitude and the length of the indices, so a small malformed
proto could cause excessive memory allocation or very deep recursion before
the HLO verifier had a chance to run.

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` now returns an `InvalidArgument` error if an
element of the original value has a shape index that does not exist in the
shape of the instruction, which bounds the size of the tree by the size of the
shape. The HLO verifier already rejects original values whose tuple structure
differs from the instruction shape, so modules that pass verification are not
affected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017201

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

head_commit.message:
Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

`Executable` takes its `HloModule` in the constructor and never changes it.
But we want `GpuExecutable` to build its module from a serialized module only
when something needs it (e.g. the profiler), and once that happened the module
should be visible through `has_module()`, `module()` and `shared_module()` like
any other module.

So this change adds a second `Executable` constructor that takes an
`HloModuleFactory` instead of a module, and `Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule`,
which returns the module and builds it with the factory if needed. The factory
is called at most once, even with concurrent callers, and if it fails every
later call returns the same error. After a successful build `has_module()`
returns true. The accessors do an acquire load of a raw pointer to the module
and only look at the `shared_ptr` once that pointer is non-null (it never
changes after that), so the read path doesn't need a lock. (We can't use
`std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>` since XLA still has to build with C++17.)

The lazy state lives in a separate heap allocation, so executables that get
their module in the constructor don't pay for it and behave exactly as before.
There is also a new `Executable(std::nullptr_t)` constructor, since
`Executable(nullptr)` would be ambiguous otherwise.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

`ShapeVerifier::HandleSort` only checked that the sort dimension is smaller
than the operand rank. Because the comparison is signed, a negative sort
dimension in an HLO module (for example one deserialized from a proto or
parsed from HLO text) passed verification. Passes and backend code
generation that run afterwards index operand shapes with the sort dimension
without further checks, which leads to out-of-bounds accesses.

The verifier now also requires the sort dimension to be non-negative, so
such modules are rejected with an error before any pass consumes them.

The error message now reports the rank of the first operand instead of
reading the dimensions of the sort result shape, which is a tuple for
sorts with more than one operand and cannot be queried for dimensions.

display_title: [XLA:LHS] Fix out-of-bounds access when no annotated node can be scheduled

head_commit.message:
[XLA:LHS] Fix out-of-bounds access when no annotated node can be scheduled

`FindAndExtractBestAnnotatedNode` removed the chosen node from the annotation
ready set by swapping it with the last element, without checking that a node
had been chosen. When every ready node of the annotation group crosses the
resource overlap limit, the iterator still points past the end of the vector,
so the swap read and wrote one element out of bounds before the caller reported
the failure.

Return early in that case and leave the ready set untouched. The caller already
turns the missing node into an error status, so scheduling such a module now
fails cleanly instead of corrupting memory.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

When matching a layer norm pattern, the operand of the reduction that calculates
the expectation may differ from the layer norm input by a reshape or bitcast
that adds or removes degenerate dimensions. `MatchLayerNorm` nevertheless used
the dimensions of the reduction to index into the shape of the input when
deriving the transpose order and the shape of the cuDNN operands. If the
reduction's operand had a higher rank than the input, this resulted in
out-of-bounds accesses of the inverse transpose order and of the input's
dimensions.

The rewrite is now skipped unless all reduction dimensions are valid dimensions
of the input and select the same non-degenerate dimensions in the input as in
the reduction's operand. Patterns for which the dimensions agree are still
rewritten.

display_title: Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

head_commit.message:
Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

`AxisRef::Validate` only checked that the mesh axis index is less than the
number of mesh axes, so a negative index, e.g. one read from an `AxisRefProto`,
passed validation. `NamedSharding` and `MeshAxesReplicaGroupList` rely on this
validation in their constructors and afterwards use the index to look up mesh
axis sizes, which resulted in an out-of-bounds read.

`AxisRef::Validate` now also returns `InvalidArgument` for negative indices.
Both constructors already `CHECK` the validation result, so a negative index is
now rejected before it is used as an index.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

head_commit.message:
PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52161

ROCm only change, This is to help us get stable address which we can use to avoid collective recapture whenever stable address is there.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

On ROCm, `--xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color` gets a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for memory space `kTempBuffer`. Next to a preallocated default pool it may use the device memory that the default pool's memory fraction leaves, like the collective pool. without preallocation it has the default pool's limit.

## 🎯 Justification

The flag assigns temp buffers to `kTempBuffer`, but only CUDA registered an allocator for that space. On ROCm, an executable whose temp allocations are combined fails:

```
INTERNAL: No allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter for device ordinal 0 and memory space 2
```

Only temp buffers use the new pool, so each execution gets the same temp address, which is what the flag is for.

- Like CUDA's pool, it sits outside the default pool: with a preallocated default pool, temp buffers must fit in what the default pool's memory fraction leaves, so a large temp buffer can run out of memory with the flag on and fit with it off. Lowering the memory fraction makes room, a fraction that leaves nothing is rejected when the client is created.
- Unlike CUDA's pool (sync mode), it does not synchronize the stream on allocate or free.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix · 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`:
- `TempBufferColorUsesSeparatePool`: a `kTempBuffer` allocation leaves the default pool untouched and gets its address back after an intervening default allocation.
- `TempBufferColorKeepsTempAddressStable`: runs an HLO whose temp allocation is recoloured; checks the results and that the temp address stays the same over three executions.

Both fail without this change with the error above.

`gpu_helpers_test` (`BfcMemorySizingTest`):
- `TempBufferPoolGetsWhatAPreallocatedPoolLeaves`: next to a default pool preallocated at 0.75 of device memory, the temp pool's limit is the remaining quarter.
- `TempBufferPoolHasDefaultLimitWithoutPreallocation`: without preallocation the temp pool keeps the default pool's limit.
- `TempBufferPoolNeedsMemoryLeftByPreallocatedPool`: a fraction of 1.0 is rejected.

`allocator_config_test`: `MemFractionTest.LeftIsWhatTheStartFractionLeaves`.

These targets pass on MI355X (ROCm 10.2); `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test` and `gpu_helpers_test` also pass on B300 (CUDA 13).

## 🧪 Execution Tests

JAX on MI355X, ROCm 10.0, with the flag on 1 GPU and on 2 GPUs with an all-reduce: results are identical to the flag off under `--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true`.

Copybara import of the project:

--
ae99d2289ba86e86f86e697855400ce89855fe2d by magaonka <magaonka@amd.com>:

[ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

- The flag puts temp buffers in memory space kTempBuffer, but only CUDA
  registered an allocator for it. On ROCm, execution failed with "No
  allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter ... memory space 2".
- On ROCm, register a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for
  kTempBuffer, named GPU_tempbuffer_<n>_bfc. Only temp buffers use it, so
  they keep the same address across executions.
- Next to a preallocated default pool, the temp pool gets the device
  memory that the default pool's start fraction leaves, like the
  collective pool; MemFractionLeft computes that remainder for both.
  Without preallocation it keeps the default pool's limit. Creating the
  client fails with a clear error if nothing is left for the temp pool.
- CreateBFCAllocator takes a name prefix (default "GPU", so existing
  pools keep GPU_<n>_bfc).
- In SharedPoolAnchorsCollectiveMemoryAtLowerEnd, convert device
  addresses to uintptr_t with reinterpret_cast instead of
  absl::bit_cast. The clang 18 static analyzer crashes comparing
  bit_cast pointer values, which fails clang-tidy on any change to
  this file.
- Update the flag's help text and add tests.

--
ee3abb0d3296b58da9517c0a1cd0b64f442a5480 by magaonka <magaonka@amd.com>:

[ROCm] Pass sub-allocator visitors to the temp buffer pool

- CreateTempBufferBFCAllocator takes the sub-allocator visitors, and the
  ROCm client passes the allocator config's, as for the default pool, so
  allocator memory registration also sees the temp pool's regions.
- Document at the call site and in the flag's help that next to a
  preallocated default pool without spatial partitioning, the separate
  collective pool gets the same limit as the temp pool and both take
  from the same remaining device memory.
- Test that the temp pool reports its regions to the visitors.

Merging this change closes #52161

display_title: In `CustomCallShardingRuleOpInterface::getShardingRule`, `CompactWyHelper`, `InvertDiagBlocksLowerTriangular`, and `InvertDiagBlocksUpperTriangular` previously used `buildPointwise`, marking their trailing two matrix dimensions as pass through instead of requiring replication. Under global to local partitioning, sharding those matrix dimensions omitted all gather reshards and executed each custom call on disjoint device slices, producing corrupted triangular inverses and Householder factors. In addition, `QrDecompositionBlock` assumed a 1 operand and 2 result real signature and crashed on 2 operand and 4 result complex decompositions, and `CustomCallPartitioningOpInterface::convertGlobalToLocal` left stale global `xla_shape` attributes on sharded custom calls.

head_commit.message:
In `CustomCallShardingRuleOpInterface::getShardingRule`, `CompactWyHelper`, `InvertDiagBlocksLowerTriangular`, and `InvertDiagBlocksUpperTriangular` previously used `buildPointwise`, marking their trailing two matrix dimensions as pass through instead of requiring replication. Under global to local partitioning, sharding those matrix dimensions omitted all gather reshards and executed each custom call on disjoint device slices, producing corrupted triangular inverses and Householder factors. In addition, `QrDecompositionBlock` assumed a 1 operand and 2 result real signature and crashed on 2 operand and 4 result complex decompositions, and `CustomCallPartitioningOpInterface::convertGlobalToLocal` left stale global `xla_shape` attributes on sharded custom calls.

Propagate leading batch dimensions pointwise and mark the trailing two matrix dimensions with `FactorType::kNeedReplication` on validated static square `CompactWyHelper` and `InvertDiagBlocks` calls, support real and complex `QrDecompositionBlock` signatures with static shape guards, and strip stale `xla_shape` attributes when localizing sharded custom calls.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Check operand element types of elementwise ops in HloEvaluator

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check operand element types of elementwise ops in HloEvaluator

`HloEvaluator` evaluates elementwise unary, binary and ternary operations, and
`rng`, by reading the values of their operands as a fixed element type, in most
cases the element type of the result. Nothing checked that the evaluated
operands actually have that element type. This is not guaranteed: the operands
of a mixed precision instruction can differ in floating point precision from
each other and from the result, and some data movement operations (e.g.
reshape) evaluate to the element type of their operand rather than their own.
The operand was then read as the wrong element type, which reads past the end
of its buffer if the actual element type is narrower.

Check the element types of the evaluated operands, once per instruction, in the
shared elementwise helpers and in `HandleRng`, and return an error on a
mismatch. Evaluating such an instruction now fails, so for example constant
folding leaves it in place, instead of computing a result from misinterpreted
data.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020056531

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add CuDnnGemmDimensions to compute the dimensions of cuDNN GEMM fusions with ShapeTracker.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add CuDnnGemmDimensions to compute the dimensions of cuDNN GEMM fusions with ShapeTracker.

`CuDnnFusionCompiler` derives the sizes and strides of the tensors of dot /
scaled-dot cuDNN fusions with `TritonFusionAnalysis`, which is part of the
legacy Triton GEMM tiling infrastructure that we want to remove: it no longer
tiles or emits fusions and does not support many of today's fusions.

`CuDnnGemmDimensions` replaces it in a follow-up change (cl/1018233906):

1.  Every instruction is related to the operand or the output of the dot that
    it contributes to by tracking the shape transformations between them with
    `ShapeTracker`.
2.  Non-scalar instructions must relate to the dot in a single way, because
    the cuDNN graph has a single tensor per instruction (e.g. `dot(p, p)` and
    `d + transpose(d)` are rejected).
3.  Sizes and strides are read from the strided view
    (`ShapeTracker::TryGetStridedView()`) of each tensor's physical layout,
    reshaped into the canonical rank-3 shape of its port, e.g. [batch, M, K].

`CudnnTensorLayout` moves to cudnn_fusion_utils.h to be shared.

display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] Warm up command buffers that contain convolutions

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] [CUDA] Warm up command buffers that contain convolutions

With CONVOLUTION in command buffers, a convolution's first execution is
recorded inside a stream capture and sets up the DNN library there: the
DNN handle, the runner and, on CUDA, the cuDNN execution plan. That
setup fails inside a capture. Make ConvolutionThunk require a warmup, as
custom calls do, so a command buffer holding a convolution runs once on
each device without recording before it is captured.

display_title: Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

head_commit.message:
Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

`AxisRef::Validate` only checked that the mesh axis index is less than the
number of mesh axes, so a negative index, e.g. one read from an `AxisRefProto`,
passed validation. `NamedSharding` and `MeshAxesReplicaGroupList` rely on this
validation in their constructors and afterwards use the index to look up mesh
axis sizes, which resulted in an out-of-bounds read.

`AxisRef::Validate` now also returns `InvalidArgument` for negative indices.
Both constructors already `CHECK` the validation result, so a negative index is
now rejected before it is used as an index.

head_commit.message:
In `CustomCallShardingRuleOpInterface::getShardingRule`, `CompactWyHelper`, `InvertDiagBlocksLowerTriangular`, and `InvertDiagBlocksUpperTriangular` previously used `buildPointwise`, marking their trailing two matrix dimensions as pass through instead of requiring replication. Under global to local partitioning, sharding those matrix dimensions omitted all gather reshards and executed each custom call on disjoint device slices, producing corrupted triangular inverses and Householder factors. In addition, `QrDecompositionBlock` assumed a 1 operand and 2 result real signature and crashed on 2 operand and 4 result complex decompositions, and `CustomCallPartitioningOpInterface::convertGlobalToLocal` left stale global `xla_shape` attributes on sharded custom calls.

Propagate leading batch dimensions pointwise and mark the trailing two matrix dimensions with `FactorType::kNeedReplication` on validated static square `CompactWyHelper` and `InvertDiagBlocks` calls, support real and complex `QrDecompositionBlock` signatures with static shape guards, and strip stale `xla_shape` attributes when localizing sharded custom calls.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Order custom interference buffers by size and reuse temp heaps

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Order custom interference buffers by size and reuse temp heaps

## Problem

Under `BufferOrder::kTopological` and `FAST_MERGE`, buffers with custom interference rules are assigned in topological or start time order rather than descending size order. When a later buffer is larger than an earlier disjoint buffer, the existing allocation is too small and a new allocation is created. In addition, `ReuseCompatibleTempHeaps` only considers allocations of other colors and cannot place movable buffers into idle custom interference allocations of the same color.

## Change

Prioritize custom interference buffers by descending size in `AssignBuffersForGlobalComputations` and cache the per-buffer custom interference and fixed offset flags before sorting. Skip `UpdateLiveness` while assigning custom interference buffers in `FastMergeBufferAllocationsManager` because `UpdateLiveness` requires buffers in increasing start time order (`CHECK_GE(current_start_time, prev_start_time_)`), whereas custom interference buffers are visited in decreasing size order ahead of normal buffers. Extend `ReuseCompatibleTempHeaps` to include reusable preallocated temporary allocations of the same color that hold custom interference buffers when placing disjoint movable buffers. Existing programs without custom interference rules do not change behavior.

## Tests

- `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service:buffer_assignment_test`: pins `CustomInterferenceTopologicalOrderConsolidatesAscendingSizes` and `ReuseCompatibleTempHeapsReusesCustomInterferenceTempOutsideLiveRange` across `SPATIAL` and `FAST_MERGE`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

Previously, the MLIR bitonic sort emitter only fused compare-and-swap steps
within one CTA's shared-memory tile (`tile_size`), requiring a separate global
kernel launch per step once `xor_mask >= tile_size`.

On Hopper+ GPUs (`sm_90+`), extend tiled bitonic sort across 2-CTA clusters
using distributed shared memory (DSMEM) and cluster barriers, doubling the
in-kernel sort span and cutting global round-trips:
- Propagate optional `se::ClusterDim` through `LaunchDimensions` and custom
  kernel specs to set driver cluster dims and `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` on kernels.
- Add `gpu::BarrierScope` (default `Workgroup`) to `xla_gpu.sync_threads`,
  forward it to `gpu.barrier` in `LowerTensors`, and lower cluster barriers to
  aligned `nvvm.cluster.arrive` and `nvvm.cluster.wait` in `LowerToLLVMGPU`.
- Support `"xla_gpu.dsmem"` on shared-memory accesses in `LowerTensors` by
  mapping the base pointer to the peer CTA's shared memory via `nvvm.mapa`.
- Emit 2-CTA clustered bitonic sort kernels when stages exceed `tile_size`,
  unclustered blocks exceed SM count, and cluster padding is at most 12.5%
  (capping at 2 CTAs avoids GPC fragmentation and register pressure). Cross-CTA
  steps use `gpu.cluster_block_id x` and DSMEM; full tiles keep the unrolled
  fast path while bounds-checked and post-cluster `kIntraTileSort` merges stay
  rolled.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013688390

display_title: PR #51750: Fix a use-after-free race in AcquireClique

head_commit.message:
PR #51750: Fix a use-after-free race in AcquireClique

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51750

📝 Summary of Changes

In AcquireClique, the rendezvous callback looks up a cached clique under state.mu, where it returns a raw LockableGpuClique* and called Acquire() after releasing the mutex. the only thing keeping the clique alive is its entry in state.cliques. Then a concurrent run on the same clique key could take state.mu, decide the clique's parent isn't a superset of its split_from, take safety_lock, erase the entry and destroy the clique. The first run would then call Acquire() on freed memory, a use-after-free.

🎯 Justification

A potential use-after-free crash

🚀 Kind of Contribution

Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix
Copybara import of the project:

--
13135fd2ec24decd11e38cba3e92afbdf1eef863 by TJ Xu <tjx@nvidia.com>:

put the owner and the lock in the same struct to keep their lifetimes the same

Merging this change closes #51750

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Don't simplify a mixed precision reduce to a reshape

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Don't simplify a mixed precision reduce to a reshape

`AlgebraicSimplifier` replaces a reduce that keeps the number of elements with
a reshape of its input. For a mixed precision reduce, whose result element type
differs from the element type of its input (e.g. an `f16` input reduced into an
`f32` result), this created a reshape whose shape has a different element type
than its operand. Such a reshape is invalid, and later passes that rely on the
declared shape, such as constant folding, could then read the operand data
using the wrong element type.

Only apply the rewrite if every result of the reduce has the same element type
as the corresponding input. Mixed precision reduces are left unchanged.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020032076

display_title: Fix cuda_clang fatbinary compression flags in embeddable_cuda_library

head_commit.message:
Fix cuda_clang fatbinary compression flags in embeddable_cuda_library

`embeddable_cuda_library` previously passed `["-no-compress", "-Xcuda-fatbinary=--compress=false"]` unconditionally in `if_oss(...)`. When building with `--@local_config_cuda//:cuda_compiler=clang` (such as TensorFlow's `build-linux-x86-cuda` CI job), `clang` rejects `-no-compress` and requires `-Xcuda-fatbinary` to be passed as two separate arguments (`["-Xcuda-fatbinary", "--compress=false"]`).

So this change selects `["-Xcuda-fatbinary", "--compress=false"]` for `@local_config_cuda//:is_cuda_compiler_clang` and `["-no-compress", "-Xcuda-fatbinary=--compress=false"]` for `@local_config_cuda//:is_cuda_compiler_nvcc`.

display_title: [XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

head_commit.message:
[XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

📝 Summary of Changes

HostOffloader::WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths follows the offloaded buffer through its users. For a generic user it keeps the same shape index, so a send user is tracked as the whole send result tuple, its send-done user is tracked as a token, and if that token is returned from the entry computation the pass ends up in the output streaming check, which does CHECK(leaf.has_layout()) on the entry result leaves. Tokens never have a layout, so the compiler aborts.

A token carries no data, so an offloaded buffer never flows through it (send-done only produces a token; the data stays in send's output {0}). This change skips token-shaped successors in the walk, and makes the output streaming check skip non-array leaves (the send result tuple itself has a token leaf, so returning the send from the entry computation hit the same CHECK). Arrays and tuples are handled exactly as before, and the existing send test (BasicHostTransferSendNoCrash) still gets its copy to host memory in front of the send.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50971. The module from the issue (MoveToHost -> send -> send-done -> ROOT tuple(send-done)) aborts GPU compilation at HEAD with "Check failed: leaf.has_layout() Expecting output shape of entry computation to have a layout." With this change it gets the same clean error as the module without the MoveToHost ("Expected recv to match send", the fuzzer module has no matching recv), and a properly paired program compiles normally.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in xla/hlo/transforms/host_offloader_test.cc. SendDoneTokenReturnedFromEntryNoCrash runs the pass on the issue's module and checks that it succeeds, that the root is still tuple(send-done(send(copy(param), after-all))), that the copy is in host memory and the parameter is not, and that no annotations remain. SendResultReturnedFromEntryNoCrash returns the send itself from the entry computation and expects a clean error (the offloaded data would be returned in a device memory output). Without the source change both tests abort with the CHECK from the issue.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added. Checked manually with run_hlo_module

head_commit.message:
PR #52733: [PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52733

Fixes jax-ml/jax#42433.

The GPU client uses stream-based usage-event compaction. In that mode `AddUsageEvent` appends any event whose definition stream isn’t known yet, and never trims the list. A copy’s source usage event is a linked promise that is only fulfilled later in `IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies`, so it always takes that path: every copy from a long-lived buffer adds one entry, and the CUDA event behind it, until the buffer is deleted.

This lets those events fall through to the trimming the non-stream branch already does: when the list is full, events that have completed (Ready or errored) are dropped before appending. A completed event has nothing left to wait for. Execute’s donation path already skips Ready events, and stream-based compaction already skips errored events when they’re added. Pending events are kept.

With the issue’s reproducer (100k `device_put` copies to `pinned_host`, RTX 4060 Ti), host memory in use went from 65.7 to 171.0 MiB before, and from 65.7 to 65.8 MiB after. New CPU, Host-platform and GPU tests fail without the change and pass with it.

Copybara import of the project:

[PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

With use_stream_based_compaction, which the GPU client sets,
AbstractTrackedDeviceBuffer::AddUsageEvent merges a new usage event into
the existing entry for its definition stream. An event whose definition
stream is not known yet is appended, and nothing in that branch ever
removes entries. Only the other branch trims events that have completed.

The source usage event of a copy is such an event. CommonCopyToMemorySpace
creates it with CreateLinkedEventPromise, and the promise is only set later
in IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies. So every CopyToMemorySpace from a
long-lived buffer, e.g. jax.device_put to another device or to pinned_host,
adds one entry, and the entries keep their CUDA events alive until the
buffer is deleted or donated. jax-ml/jax#42433 measured about 1.1 KB of
host memory per copy and source shard, without a plateau.

When the vector is full, drop the entries that are Ready before appending,
like the other branch does. A Ready usage event has completed without an
error, so Delete and the donation paths have nothing left to wait for, and
Execute already skips Ready usage events when it donates a buffer. Pending
and errored entries are kept, so per-stream merging and error propagation
do not change.

trimming the other mode already does, instead of a copy of it. The trim
checks the event state through the device event interface rather than
async_value(), which is null for events that aren't local AsyncValues.

Merging this change closes #52733

display_title: Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

A GpuExecutable that only keeps the serialized HloModule (see `GpuExecutable::GetOrCreateHloModule`) has no module for two profiler features: the per-instruction trace annotations and the debug info that XlaDebugInfoManager hands out at the end of a trace. Building the module at construction time just for that would defeat the point of not keeping it around.

So this change builds the module on the first execution that sees an active profiler (through the new `MaybePrepareProfiling`). That execution and all later ones use the full annotations prepared from the module instead of the name-only ones, and the module gets registered with XlaDebugInfoManager like any other module. (If the module was already built for another reason, we use that one.) Without a profiler nothing changes, so the module is never built. If building the module fails, we log a warning once and keep using the name-only annotations.

Executables that have an HloModule behave exactly as before.

display_title: Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

head_commit.message:
Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

A deserialized GpuExecutable still needs the HLO module to compute the module fingerprint and to decide whether collectives should use minimal GPU resources. Both are pure functions of the optimized module, so we can compute them at compile time and store them in `GpuExecutableProto` (xla/service/gpu/gpu_executable.proto) instead.

This change adds the `fingerprint` and `collective_use_minimal_resource` fields, writes them in `ToProto` and uses them in `FromProto`. `GpuExecutable::Create` computes the fingerprint from the module unless it's passed in, which happens when deserializing and when the compiler doesn't embed the module. Executables serialized before these fields existed fall back to computing the values from the HLO module, which is still deserialized eagerly for now. Executables without an HLO module have an empty fingerprint and always write `collective_use_minimal_resource=false`, which is the value they used before. If `Params::hlo_module` only holds the serialized module (nothing does that yet), `Create` requires `collective_use_minimal_resource` to be set, because we don't want to build the module just for that and silently using false could differ from what the module would give.

Computing the fingerprint eagerly costs 0.1-0.45% of the JIT compile time (measured on H100 for gemma4_2b, maxtext and a chain of 500 dots, with and without autotuning). That's cheap enough to not justify a lazily computed and cached value.

The fingerprint stored at compile time matches the fingerprint of the module after a serialization round trip (which is what PjRt computed for deserialized executables so far). A new PjRt test checks that for a few non-trivial programs, and I also verified it for all GPU AOT goldens.

The AOT golden comparison ignores both fields since they are derived from the HLO module, which is already ignored.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
new `GpuExecutable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

All of this lives in `GpuExecutable`, `Executable` only sees the module through
the virtual accessors. The build-once state (mutex, factory, sticky error and
the built module) is in a separate heap-allocated struct, so executables
without a serialized module don't pay for it. Readers like `shared_module()`
don't take the lock. Until the module is built, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the
serialized module (the config with the same debug options the built module
gets) and from the output info, so asking for them doesn't build the module.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

head_commit.message:
Fix cuda_clang fatbinary compression flags in embeddable_cuda_library

`embeddable_cuda_library` previously passed `["-no-compress", "-Xcuda-fatbinary=--compress=false"]` unconditionally in `if_oss(...)`. name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Don't simplify a mixed precision reduce to a reshape

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Don't simplify a mixed precision reduce to a reshape

`AlgebraicSimplifier` replaces a reduce that keeps the number of elements with
a reshape of its input. For a mixed precision reduce, whose result element type
differs from the element type of its input (e.g. an `f16` input reduced into an
`f32` result), this created a reshape whose shape has a different element type
than its operand. Such a reshape is invalid, and later passes that rely on the
declared shape, such as constant folding, could then read the operand data
using the wrong element type.

Only apply the rewrite if every result of the reduce has the same element type
as the corresponding input. Mixed precision reduces are left unchanged.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Check operand element types of elementwise ops in HloEvaluator

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check operand element types of elementwise ops in HloEvaluator

`HloEvaluator` evaluates elementwise unary, binary and ternary operations, and
`rng`, by reading the values of their operands as a fixed element type, in most
cases the element type of the result. Nothing checked that the evaluated
operands actually have that element type. This is not guaranteed: the operands
of a mixed precision instruction can differ in floating point precision from
each other and from the result, and some data movement operations (e.g.
reshape) evaluate to the element type of their operand rather than their own.
The operand was then read as the wrong element type, which reads past the end
of its buffer if the actual element type is narrower.

Check the element types of the evaluated operands, once per instruction, in the
shared elementwise helpers and in `HandleRng`, and return an error on a
mismatch. Evaluating such an instruction now fails, so for example constant
folding leaves it in place, instead of computing a result from misinterpreted
data.

head_commit.message:
PR #52733: [PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52733

Fixes jax-ml/jax#42433.

The GPU client uses stream-based usage-event compaction. In that mode `AddUsageEvent` appends any event whose definition stream isn’t known yet, and never trims the list. A copy’s source usage event is a linked promise that is only fulfilled later in `IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies`, so it always takes that path: every copy from a long-lived buffer adds one entry, and the CUDA event behind it, until the buffer is deleted.

This lets those events fall through to the trimming the non-stream branch already does: when the list is full, events that have completed (Ready or errored) are dropped before appending. A completed event has nothing left to wait for. Execute’s donation path already skips Ready events, and stream-based compaction already skips errored events when they’re added. Pending events are kept.

With the issue’s reproducer (100k `device_put` copies to `pinned_host`, RTX 4060 Ti), host memory in use went from 65.7 to 171.0 MiB before, and from 65.7 to 65.8 MiB after. New CPU, Host-platform and GPU tests fail without the change and pass with it.

f71825ada9572b7d1881fd219089b85501ea2bab by JonSnow1807 <JonSnow1807@users.noreply.github.com>:

[PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

With use_stream_based_compaction, which the GPU client sets,
AbstractTrackedDeviceBuffer::AddUsageEvent merges a new usage event into
the existing entry for its definition stream. An event whose definition
stream is not known yet is appended, and nothing in that branch ever
removes entries. Only the other branch trims events that have completed.

The source usage event of a copy is such an event. CommonCopyToMemorySpace
creates it with CreateLinkedEventPromise, and the promise is only set later
in IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies. So every CopyToMemorySpace from a
long-lived buffer, e.g. jax.device_put to another device or to pinned_host,
adds one entry, and the entries keep their CUDA events alive until the
buffer is deleted or donated. jax-ml/jax#42433 measured about 1.1 KB of
host memory per copy and source shard, without a plateau.

When the vector is full, drop the entries that are Ready before appending,
like the other branch does. A Ready usage event has completed without an
error, so Delete and the donation paths have nothing left to wait for, and
Execute already skips Ready usage events when it donates a buffer. Pending
and errored entries are kept, so per-stream merging and error propagation
do not change.

`embeddable_cuda_library` previously passed `["-no-compress", "-Xcuda-fatbinary=--compress=false"]` unconditionally in `if_oss(...)`. today), no golden holds the executable that a default compile emits.

display_title: PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

head_commit.message:
PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52161

ROCm only change, This is to help us get stable address which we can use to avoid collective recapture whenever stable address is there.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

On ROCm, `--xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color` gets a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for memory space `kTempBuffer`. Next to a preallocated default pool it may use the device memory that the default pool's memory fraction leaves, like the collective pool. without preallocation it has the default pool's limit.

## 🎯 Justification

The flag assigns temp buffers to `kTempBuffer`, but only CUDA registered an allocator for that space. On ROCm, an executable whose temp allocations are combined fails:

```
INTERNAL: No allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter for device ordinal 0 and memory space 2
```

Only temp buffers use the new pool, so each execution gets the same temp address, which is what the flag is for.

- Like CUDA's pool, it sits outside the default pool: with a preallocated default pool, temp buffers must fit in what the default pool's memory fraction leaves, so a large temp buffer can run out of memory with the flag on and fit with it off. Lowering the memory fraction makes room, a fraction that leaves nothing is rejected when the client is created.
- Unlike CUDA's pool (sync mode), it does not synchronize the stream on allocate or free.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix · 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`:
- `TempBufferColorUsesSeparatePool`: a `kTempBuffer` allocation leaves the default pool untouched and gets its address back after an intervening default allocation.
- `TempBufferColorKeepsTempAddressStable`: runs an HLO whose temp allocation is recoloured; checks the results and that the temp address stays the same over three executions.

Both fail without this change with the error above.

`gpu_helpers_test` (`BfcMemorySizingTest`):
- `TempBufferPoolGetsWhatAPreallocatedPoolLeaves`: next to a default pool preallocated at 0.75 of device memory, the temp pool's limit is the remaining quarter.
- `TempBufferPoolHasDefaultLimitWithoutPreallocation`: without preallocation the temp pool keeps the default pool's limit.
- `TempBufferPoolNeedsMemoryLeftByPreallocatedPool`: a fraction of 1.0 is rejected.

`allocator_config_test`: `MemFractionTest.LeftIsWhatTheStartFractionLeaves`.

These targets pass on MI355X (ROCm 10.2); `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test` and `gpu_helpers_test` also pass on B300 (CUDA 13).

## 🧪 Execution Tests

JAX on MI355X, ROCm 10.0, with the flag on 1 GPU and on 2 GPUs with an all-reduce: results are identical to the flag off under `--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true`.

Copybara import of the project:

--
ae99d2289ba86e86f86e697855400ce89855fe2d by magaonka <magaonka@amd.com>:

[ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

- The flag puts temp buffers in memory space kTempBuffer, but only CUDA
  registered an allocator for it. On ROCm, execution failed with "No
  allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter ... memory space 2".
- On ROCm, register a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for
  kTempBuffer, named GPU_tempbuffer_<n>_bfc. Only temp buffers use it, so
  they keep the same address across executions.
- Next to a preallocated default pool, the temp pool gets the device
  memory that the default pool's start fraction leaves, like the
  collective pool; MemFractionLeft computes that remainder for both.
  Without preallocation it keeps the default pool's limit. Creating the
  client fails with a clear error if nothing is left for the temp pool.
- CreateBFCAllocator takes a name prefix (default "GPU", so existing
  pools keep GPU_<n>_bfc).
- In SharedPoolAnchorsCollectiveMemoryAtLowerEnd, convert device
  addresses to uintptr_t with reinterpret_cast instead of
  absl::bit_cast. The clang 18 static analyzer crashes comparing
  bit_cast pointer values, which fails clang-tidy on any change to
  this file.
- Update the flag's help text and add tests.

[ROCm] Pass sub-allocator visitors to the temp buffer pool

- CreateTempBufferBFCAllocator takes the sub-allocator visitors, and the
  ROCm client passes the allocator config's, as for the default pool, so
  allocator memory registration also sees the temp pool's regions.
- Document at the call site and in the flag's help that next to a
  preallocated default pool without spatial partitioning, the separate
  collective pool gets the same limit as the temp pool and both take
  from the same remaining device memory.
- Test that the temp pool reports its regions to the visitors.

Merging this change closes #52161

display_title: [XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

head_commit.message:
[XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

📝 Summary of Changes

HostOffloader::WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths follows the offloaded buffer through its users. For a generic user it keeps the same shape index, so a send user is tracked as the whole send result tuple, its send-done user is tracked as a token, and if that token is returned from the entry computation the pass ends up in the output streaming check, which does CHECK(leaf.has_layout()) on the entry result leaves. Tokens never have a layout, so the compiler aborts.

A token carries no data, so an offloaded buffer never flows through it (send-done only produces a token; the data stays in send's output {0}). Arrays and tuples are handled exactly as before, and the existing send test (BasicHostTransferSendNoCrash) still gets its copy to host memory in front of the send.

Fixes #50971. The module from the issue (MoveToHost -> send -> send-done -> ROOT tuple(send-done)) aborts GPU compilation at HEAD with "Check failed: leaf.has_layout() Expecting output shape of entry computation to have a layout." With this change it gets the same clean error as the module without the MoveToHost ("Expected recv to match send", the fuzzer module has no matching recv), and a properly paired program compiles normally.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in xla/hlo/transforms/host_offloader_test.cc. SendDoneTokenReturnedFromEntryNoCrash runs the pass on the issue's module and checks that it succeeds, that the root is still tuple(send-done(send(copy(param), after-all))), that the copy is in host memory and the parameter is not, and that no annotations remain. SendResultReturnedFromEntryNoCrash returns the send itself from the entry computation and expects a clean error (the offloaded data would be returned in a device memory output). None added. Checked manually with run_hlo_module

head_commit.message:
PR #52733: [PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52733

Fixes jax-ml/jax#42433.

The GPU client uses stream-based usage-event compaction. In that mode `AddUsageEvent` appends any event whose definition stream isn’t known yet, and never trims the list. A copy’s source usage event is a linked promise that is only fulfilled later in `IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies`, so it always takes that path: every copy from a long-lived buffer adds one entry, and the CUDA event behind it, until the buffer is deleted.

This lets those events fall through to the trimming the non-stream branch already does: when the list is full, events that have completed (Ready or errored) are dropped before appending. A completed event has nothing left to wait for. Execute’s donation path already skips Ready events, and stream-based compaction already skips errored events when they’re added. Pending events are kept.

With the issue’s reproducer (100k `device_put` copies to `pinned_host`, RTX 4060 Ti), host memory in use went from 65.7 to 171.0 MiB before, and from 65.7 to 65.8 MiB after. New CPU, Host-platform and GPU tests fail without the change and pass with it.

Copybara import of the project:

f71825ada9572b7d1881fd219089b85501ea2bab by JonSnow1807 <JonSnow1807@users.noreply.github.com>:

[PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

With use_stream_based_compaction, which the GPU client sets,
AbstractTrackedDeviceBuffer::AddUsageEvent merges a new usage event into
the existing entry for its definition stream. An event whose definition
stream is not known yet is appended, and nothing in that branch ever
removes entries. Only the other branch trims events that have completed.

The source usage event of a copy is such an event. CommonCopyToMemorySpace
creates it with CreateLinkedEventPromise, and the promise is only set later
in IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies. So every CopyToMemorySpace from a
long-lived buffer, e.g. jax.device_put to another device or to pinned_host,
adds one entry, and the entries keep their CUDA events alive until the
buffer is deleted or donated. jax-ml/jax#42433 measured about 1.1 KB of
host memory per copy and source shard, without a plateau.

When the vector is full, drop the entries that are Ready before appending,
like the other branch does. A Ready usage event has completed without an
error, so Delete and the donation paths have nothing left to wait for, and
Execute already skips Ready usage events when it donates a buffer. Pending
and errored entries are kept, so per-stream merging and error propagation
do not change.

checks the event state through the device event interface rather than
async_value(), which is null for events that aren't local AsyncValues.
