display_title: Make the HloModule metadata accessors of Executable virtual

head_commit.message:
Make the HloModule metadata accessors of Executable virtual

`Executable` owns the `HloModule` it was compiled from and reads all module
metadata from it. We want backends to be able to keep the module themselves (or
not at all), and `GpuExecutable` in particular shouldn't need the module to
answer simple questions like "what's the aliasing of the entry computation".

So this change makes `shared_module()` and `module_config()` virtual and adds
virtual `input_output_alias_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()`. `module()`
and `has_module()` stay non-virtual and go through a new protected virtual
`module_ptr()`, so that subclasses that keep their own module only have to
override `shared_module()` and `module_ptr()`. All defaults read the module the
base class holds, so nothing changes for any backend.

I also removed `execution_count_`, which nothing used anymore.

display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
new `GpuExecutable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

All of this lives in `GpuExecutable`, `Executable` only sees the module through
the virtual accessors. The build-once state (mutex, factory, sticky error and
the built module) is in a separate heap-allocated struct, so executables
without a serialized module don't pay for it. Readers like `shared_module()`
don't take the lock. Until the module is built, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the
serialized module (the config with the same debug options the built module
gets) and from the output info, so asking for them doesn't build the module.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

display_title: Let GpuExecutable own its HloModule and answer metadata queries without it

head_commit.message:
Let GpuExecutable own its HloModule and answer metadata queries without it

`GpuExecutable` now keeps its optional `HloModule` itself instead of passing it
to `Executable`, and overrides `shared_module()`, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()`.

If the executable has the module, these return the module's values, exactly as
before. Without the module (`embed_hlo_module=false`, or a `GpuExecutableProto`
without a serialized module), the executable answers from what it keeps:

- The input/output aliasing is rebuilt from the output info, which is already
  part of `GpuExecutableProto`.
- `module_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the new
  `GpuExecutable::Params::module_config` and `Params::buffer_donor_config`,
  which `GpuCompiler` fills from the module when it doesn't embed it.
  `module_config()` still CHECK-fails if neither is there, as today.

This way callers can get the metadata of an executable compiled with
`embed_hlo_module=false` through the `Executable` interface.

head_commit.message:
Fix cuda_clang fatbinary compression flags in embeddable_cuda_library

`embeddable_cuda_library` previously passed `["-no-compress", "-Xcuda-fatbinary=--compress=false"]` unconditionally in `if_oss(...)`. When building with `--@local_config_cuda//:cuda_compiler=clang` (such as TensorFlow's `build-linux-x86-cuda` CI job), `clang` rejects `-no-compress` and requires `-Xcuda-fatbinary` to be passed as two separate arguments (`["-Xcuda-fatbinary", "--compress=false"]`).

display_title: PR #52698: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputStream

head_commit.message:
PR #52698: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputStream

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52698

#ai-generated

**Status quo**: `SnappyInputStream::ReadNBytes` passes its `int64_t bytes_to_read` straight to `resize_uninitialized`, which takes a `size_t`. A count of -1 reaches the __builtin_trap in TF_TString_ResizeUninitialized and the process dies with SIGILL; other negative counts convert to a `size_t` of 2^63 or more. BufferedInputStream::ReadNBytes and RandomAccessInputStream::ReadNBytes return `InvalidArgument` for a negative count.

**Why**: This is the small separate change suggested in #52502, where the `SnappyInputStream` behavior was identified as the root cause of the crash seen through RecordReader on Snappy-compressed files. The streams should reject a negative count the same way.

**Design choices**: `ReadNBytes` returns `InvalidArgument("Can't read a negative number of bytes: <n>")` before it touches `result`, matching the message in BufferedInputStream. It uses `absl::InvalidArgumentError(absl::StrCat(...))`, as BufferedInputStream does, because `errors::InvalidArgument` is deprecated. The `absl::Cord` overload calls this one, so it is covered too. No other production file changes.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives**: This only rejects negative counts. A large positive count still allocates `bytes_to_read` bytes up front, as the other streams do; bounding that would be a separate change. RecordReader is left as is, per the discussion in #52502.

**Testing**: `InputStreamRejectsNegativeBytesToRead` (`ReadNBytes(-1, ...)` returns `InvalidArgument`) crashes `snappy_test` without the change and passes with it. The `snappy_test` binary (13 tests) passes in full with the change in an optimized build and an ASan build on Linux x86_64.

AI assistance was used in drafting and validating this change; the patch and tests were reviewed and verified by the author.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

GemmFusion special-cased a fusion output that is the root of its computation: it set the new root by hand and removed the old instruction instead of calling `ReplaceInstruction`. Every other output goes through `ReplaceInstruction`, which also carries the replaced instruction's frontend attributes, metadata and control dependencies over to the replacement. The fusion, or the bitcast that replaces the output, therefore inherited those only when the replaced instruction was not the root.

`ReplaceInstruction` already updates the computation root, so the special case is not needed. Remove it so that root and non-root outputs are replaced the same way.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject shardings with more last_tile_dims than tile assignment dimensions

`HloSharding::Subgroup` assumes that the number of subgroup types does not
exceed the rank of the tile assignment. Neither `HloSharding::FromProto` nor
the HLO text parser enforced this for `last_tile_dims`, so a malformed
`OpSharding` proto or sharding string made the computed number of data
dimensions negative and crashed the process.

Validate this where the sharding is deserialized: `HloSharding::FromProto` now
returns an error status and the HLO parser reports a parse error.

The source usage event of a copy is such an event. CommonCopyToMemorySpace
creates it with CreateLinkedEventPromise, and the promise is only set later
in IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies. So every CopyToMemorySpace from a
long-lived buffer, e.g. jax.device_put to another device or to pinned_host,
adds one entry, and the entries keep their CUDA events alive until the
buffer is deleted or donated. jax-ml/jax#42433 measured about 1.1 KB of
host memory per copy and source shard, without a plateau.

When the vector is full, drop the entries that are Ready before appending,
like the other branch does. A Ready usage event has completed without an
error, so Delete and the donation paths have nothing left to wait for, and
Execute already skips Ready usage events when it donates a buffer. Pending
and errored entries are kept, so per-stream merging and error propagation
do not change.

Annotation emission is strictly best-effort and never fails a job.
- Enable `--build_event_json_file=build_events.json` in `build_tools/ci/build.py` (`_DEFAULT_BAZEL_OPTIONS`), invoke `bep_annotations` on final Bazel failure or interrupt in GitHub Actions (covering `ci.yml` and `ci_multi_device.yml`), upload `build_events.json` in `ci.yml` failure artifacts, and update `golden_commands.txt` and `build_test.py`.
- Add best-effort (`continue-on-error: true`, `if: failure() || cancelled()`) annotation steps to `.github/workflows/rocm_ci.yml` for both the JAX and XLA jobs.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Optimize packed transpose codegen and vector alignment.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Optimize packed transpose codegen and vector alignment.

***Problem:*** Unaligned vector transfer lowering and scalar elementwise shared-memory extraction split 32-bit packed loads and stores into narrow memory operations, inflate sub-byte vector SelectionDAG legalization, and under-occupy packed transpose blocks.

***Solution:*** Infer byte alignment from base buffers and affine index divisors, lower aligned power-of-two sub-byte vector transfers through wide integer loads and stores, and transpose 32-bit packed shared-memory tiles with an in-register `i32` butterfly at 256 threads per block.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Model dot shared-memory pipe throughput and cp.async bank conflicts.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model dot shared-memory pipe throughput and cp.async bank conflicts.

Pipelined dot mainloops previously did not account for shared-memory bandwidth.
When a >=32-bit dot operand cannot vectorize async global-to-shared loads along
its minor dimension (due to a non-unit tile stride or odd dimension size) and
its padded minor tile size does not exceed the thread count, Triton uses an
unswizzled transposed shared-memory layout that suffers bank conflicts.

Bounding multi-stage, multi-iteration K-loops by SM shared-memory throughput
(including bank-conflict serialization) ensures the cost model does not
underprice pipelined tiles bottlenecked on shared memory.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

GemmFusion special-cased a fusion output that is the root of its computation: it set the new root by hand and removed the old instruction instead of calling `ReplaceInstruction`. Every other output goes through `ReplaceInstruction`, which also carries the replaced instruction's frontend attributes, metadata and control dependencies over to the replacement. The fusion, or the bitcast that replaces the output, therefore inherited those only when the replaced instruction was not the root.

`ReplaceInstruction` already updates the computation root, so the special case is not needed. Remove it so that root and non-root outputs are replaced the same way.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

The collective pattern matchers evaluate table lookups, i.e. a dynamic-slice
of a rank-1 constant indexed by a device id or by another table lookup, at
compile time. The index was only checked for being non-negative before it was
used to read the constant's literal, and the literal accessors only validate
indices with `DCHECK`. A module whose replica groups or tables yield an index
past the end of a table therefore caused an out-of-bounds read in optimized
builds.

Route all four table reads (`GetIndexForId`, `IsPerIdOffsets`,
`EvaluateOffset` and `GetIndicesSpecForDynamicSlice`) through a single
`GetTableEntry` helper that returns `nullopt` when the index is outside the
constant table, so that the pattern simply does not match. Lookups into iota
tables are unchanged since they do not read a literal.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019939483

display_title: PR #52787: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputBuffer

head_commit.message:
PR #52787: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputBuffer

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52787

#ai-generated

**Status quo:** `SnappyInputBuffer::ReadNBytes` passes its `int64_t bytes_to_read` straight to `resize_uninitialized`, which takes a `size_t`. A count of -1 reaches the __builtin_trap in TF_TString_ResizeUninitialized and the process dies with SIGILL; other negative counts convert to a `size_t` of 2^63 or more. BufferedInputStream::ReadNBytes and RandomAccessInputStream::ReadNBytes return `InvalidArgument` for a negative count.

**Why:** In #52502 the missing negative-count check in SnappyInputStream::ReadNBytes was identified as the root cause of the crash seen through RecordReader, and a small separate PR adding the check was welcome so the streams behave consistently. #52698 does that for SnappyInputStream. `SnappyInputBuffer` is the other Snappy InputStreamInterface implementation in the same directory and has the same unchecked call, so this makes it consistent too.

**Design choices:** `ReadNBytes` returns `InvalidArgument("Can't read a negative number of bytes: <n>")` as its first statement, before `result` is cleared or resized, matching the message in BufferedInputStream. It uses `absl::InvalidArgumentError(absl::StrCat(...))`, as BufferedInputStream does, because `errors::InvalidArgument` is deprecated. The test lives in a new `snappy_inputbuffer_test.cc` with its own `snappy_inputbuffer_test` target, so `snappy_test.cc` (which #52698 edits) is not touched.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives:** This only rejects negative counts. A large positive count still allocates `bytes_to_read` bytes up front, as the other streams do; bounding that would be a separate change. There is no new positive-control test because SnappyBuffers.Tell in `snappy_test` already covers positive reads through `SnappyInputBuffer`. ZlibInputStream is left as is.

**Testing:** `SnappyInputBuffer.RejectsNegativeBytesToRead` calls `ReadNBytes(-1, ...)` and expects `InvalidArgument`. It crashes with SIGILL without the change and passes with it, in a default optimized build and an ASan build on Linux x86_64. The existing `snappy_test` (12 tests) passes with and without the change in both builds.

AI assistance was used in drafting and validating this change; the patch and tests were reviewed and verified by the author.

display_title: [XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

The collective pattern matchers evaluate table lookups, i.e. a dynamic-slice
of a rank-1 constant indexed by a device id or by another table lookup, at
compile time. The index was only checked for being non-negative before it was
used to read the constant's literal, and the literal accessors only validate
indices with `DCHECK`. A module whose replica groups or tables yield an index
past the end of a table therefore caused an out-of-bounds read in optimized
builds.

Route all four table reads (`GetIndexForId`, `IsPerIdOffsets`,
`EvaluateOffset` and `GetIndicesSpecForDynamicSlice`) through a single
`GetTableEntry` helper that returns `nullopt` when the index is outside the
constant table, so that the pattern simply does not match. Lookups into iota
tables are unchanged since they do not read a literal.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019018870

head_commit.message:
PR #52787: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputBuffer

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52787

#ai-generated

**Status quo:** `SnappyInputBuffer::ReadNBytes` passes its `int64_t bytes_to_read` straight to `resize_uninitialized`, which takes a `size_t`. A count of -1 reaches the __builtin_trap in TF_TString_ResizeUninitialized and the process dies with SIGILL; other negative counts convert to a `size_t` of 2^63 or more. BufferedInputStream::ReadNBytes and RandomAccessInputStream::ReadNBytes return `InvalidArgument` for a negative count.

**Why:** In #52502 the missing negative-count check in SnappyInputStream::ReadNBytes was identified as the root cause of the crash seen through RecordReader, and a small separate PR adding the check was welcome so the streams behave consistently. #52698 does that for SnappyInputStream. `SnappyInputBuffer` is the other Snappy InputStreamInterface implementation in the same directory and has the same unchecked call, so this makes it consistent too.

**Design choices:** `ReadNBytes` returns `InvalidArgument("Can't read a negative number of bytes: <n>")` as its first statement, before `result` is cleared or resized, matching the message in BufferedInputStream. It uses `absl::InvalidArgumentError(absl::StrCat(...))`, as BufferedInputStream does, because `errors::InvalidArgument` is deprecated. The test lives in a new `snappy_inputbuffer_test.cc` with its own `snappy_inputbuffer_test` target, so `snappy_test.cc` (which #52698 edits) is not touched.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives:** This only rejects negative counts. A large positive count still allocates `bytes_to_read` bytes up front, as the other streams do; bounding that would be a separate change. There is no new positive-control test because SnappyBuffers.Tell in `snappy_test` already covers positive reads through `SnappyInputBuffer`. ZlibInputStream is left as is.

**Testing:** `SnappyInputBuffer.RejectsNegativeBytesToRead` calls `ReadNBytes(-1, ...)` and expects `InvalidArgument`. It crashes with SIGILL without the change and passes with it, in a default optimized build and an ASan build on Linux x86_64. The existing `snappy_test` (12 tests) passes with and without the change in both builds.

AI assistance was used in drafting and validating this change; the patch and tests were reviewed and verified by the author.

display_title: Fix GPU collective-permute cycle decomposer for multiple cycles.

head_commit.message:
Fix GPU collective-permute cycle decomposer for multiple cycles.

`DecomposeCollectivePermuteCycle` recombines the backward and forward collective-permutes using a `select` predicate that previously compared the partition or replica ID only against `back_pairs.back().second` (the last back-edge target). When `source_target_pairs` contains multiple disjoint cycles, `GetCycleTypeAndIndices` breaks out one back edge per cycle into `back_pairs`, so every back-edge receiver except the last routed through the forward collective-permute (where it is not a target) and read zeros instead of its permuted data.

Compare the partition or replica ID against every target in `back_pairs` and combine the equality predicates with `or` so all back-edge receivers select the backward collective-permute, leaving single-cycle HLO output unchanged. Verified with multi-cycle forward and backward unit tests in `CollectivePermuteCycleDecomposerTest`.

Based on https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46248 by @Ashutosh0x.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

For grouped matmuls `CublasLtMatmulThunk::ExecuteOnStream` reads the
`group_sizes` buffer, but `buffer_uses()` did not list it. Command buffers rely
on `buffer_uses()` to determine which buffer allocations a recorded command
depends on, so a change of only the `group_sizes` device address between
executions went unnoticed and the previously recorded command could be replayed
with a stale address.

Report `group_sizes` as a read buffer use when it is present, so that command
buffer update tracking and the traced command buffer cache account for it.
Regular (non-grouped) matmuls are unaffected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019918987

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

head_commit.message:
[CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

`ChloOpRecomposePattern` moves the regions of a `stablehlo.composite` into the
CHLO op it creates by zipping both region lists with `llvm::zip_equal`.
`stablehlo.composite` accepts any number of regions, while the CHLO ops have a
fixed number, and nothing checked that the two agree. `zip_equal` only asserts
on equal lengths; without assertions it iterates over the composite's regions,
so a composite with more regions than the CHLO op made the pattern access
regions past the end of the new op, and one with fewer left the new op with an
empty region.

Compare the region counts before moving the regions and fail the match when
they differ, erasing the op that was just created so the IR is left unchanged.
Such a composite is then left in place, like any other composite that the
pass does not recompose.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019918744

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

`ThunkEmitter::EmitConstant` stored the number of elements of a constant in an
`int`. For constants with 2^31 or more elements the count wrapped around, so
such a constant could be mistaken for a scalar: its global was sized as the
64 byte minimum allocation and `AppendGlobalConstant` copied the whole
content into the fixed 64 byte padding buffer, writing past its end.

Keep the element count as `int64_t`, so that only constants with at most one
element get an inline initializer, and only fill the padding buffer when the
content is actually smaller than the minimum allocation.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019916668

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Drop removed instructions from the HloCSE representative set

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Drop removed instructions from the HloCSE representative set

HloCSE can remove an instruction that it has already recorded as the
representative of its equivalence class: a duplicate iota operand of the
instruction being visited, or an operand that becomes unused when a duplicate
instruction is replaced. The removed instruction stayed in the set, so an
equivalent instruction visited later was replaced with it. That left live
instructions with an operand that is no longer part of the computation and
that is deleted when the module is cleaned up.

Erase such instructions from the set before they are removed. The extra
lookup only happens for instructions that HloCSE removes in addition to the
duplicate it is replacing, so the common path is unchanged.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019915469

display_title: PR #52698: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputStream

head_commit.message:
PR #52698: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputStream

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52698

#ai-generated

**Status quo**: `SnappyInputStream::ReadNBytes` passes its `int64_t bytes_to_read` straight to `resize_uninitialized`, which takes a `size_t`. A count of -1 reaches the __builtin_trap in TF_TString_ResizeUninitialized and the process dies with SIGILL; other negative counts convert to a `size_t` of 2^63 or more. BufferedInputStream::ReadNBytes and RandomAccessInputStream::ReadNBytes return `InvalidArgument` for a negative count.

**Why**: This is the small separate change suggested in #52502, where the `SnappyInputStream` behavior was identified as the root cause of the crash seen through RecordReader on Snappy-compressed files. The streams should reject a negative count the same way.

**Design choices**: `ReadNBytes` returns `InvalidArgument("Can't read a negative number of bytes: <n>")` before it touches `result`, matching the message in BufferedInputStream. It uses `absl::InvalidArgumentError(absl::StrCat(...))`, as BufferedInputStream does, because `errors::InvalidArgument` is deprecated. The `absl::Cord` overload calls this one, so it is covered too. No other production file changes.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives**: This only rejects negative counts. A large positive count still allocates `bytes_to_read` bytes up front, as the other streams do; bounding that would be a separate change. RecordReader is left as is, per the discussion in #52502.

**Testing**: `InputStreamRejectsNegativeBytesToRead` (`ReadNBytes(-1, ...)` returns `InvalidArgument`) crashes `snappy_test` without the change and passes with it. The `snappy_test` binary (13 tests) passes in full with the change in an optimized build and an ASan build on Linux x86_64.

AI assistance was used in drafting and validating this change; the patch and tests were reviewed and verified by the author.

display_title: [XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

The collective pattern matchers evaluate table lookups, i.e. a dynamic-slice
of a rank-1 constant indexed by a device id or by another table lookup, at
compile time. The index was only checked for being non-negative before it was
used to read the constant's literal, and the literal accessors only validate
indices with `DCHECK`. A module whose replica groups or tables yield an index
past the end of a table therefore caused an out-of-bounds read in optimized
builds.

Route all four table reads (`GetIndexForId`, `IsPerIdOffsets`,
`EvaluateOffset` and `GetIndicesSpecForDynamicSlice`) through a single
`GetTableEntry` helper that returns `nullopt` when the index is outside the
constant table, so that the pattern simply does not match. Lookups into iota
tables are unchanged since they do not read a literal.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019018870

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

GemmFusion special-cased a fusion output that is the root of its computation: it set the new root by hand and removed the old instruction instead of calling `ReplaceInstruction`. Every other output goes through `ReplaceInstruction`, which also carries the replaced instruction's frontend attributes, metadata and control dependencies over to the replacement. The fusion, or the bitcast that replaces the output, therefore inherited those only when the replaced instruction was not the root.

`ReplaceInstruction` already updates the computation root, so the special case is not needed. Remove it so that root and non-root outputs are replaced the same way.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019065033

display_title: [XLA] Drop removed instructions from the HloCSE representative set

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Drop removed instructions from the HloCSE representative set

HloCSE can remove an instruction that it has already recorded as the
representative of its equivalence class: a duplicate iota operand of the
instruction being visited, or an operand that becomes unused when a duplicate
instruction is replaced. The removed instruction stayed in the set, so an
equivalent instruction visited later was replaced with it. That left live
instructions with an operand that is no longer part of the computation and
that is deleted when the module is cleaned up.

Erase such instructions from the set before they are removed. The extra
lookup only happens for instructions that HloCSE removes in addition to the
duplicate it is replacing, so the common path is unchanged.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017214

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

`ThunkEmitter::EmitConstant` stored the number of elements of a constant in an
`int`. For constants with 2^31 or more elements the count wrapped around, so
such a constant could be mistaken for a scalar: its global was sized as the
64 byte minimum allocation and `AppendGlobalConstant` copied the whole
content into the fixed 64 byte padding buffer, writing past its end.

Keep the element count as `int64_t`, so that only constants with at most one
element get an inline initializer, and only fill the padding buffer when the
content is actually smaller than the minimum allocation.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

For grouped matmuls `CublasLtMatmulThunk::ExecuteOnStream` reads the
`group_sizes` buffer, but `buffer_uses()` did not list it. Command buffers rely
on `buffer_uses()` to determine which buffer allocations a recorded command
depends on, so a change of only the `group_sizes` device address between
executions went unnoticed and the previously recorded command could be replayed
with a stale address.

Report `group_sizes` as a read buffer use when it is present, so that command
buffer update tracking and the traced command buffer cache account for it.
Regular (non-grouped) matmuls are unaffected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019015197

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

head_commit.message:
[CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

`ChloOpRecomposePattern` moves the regions of a `stablehlo.composite` into the
CHLO op it creates by zipping both region lists with `llvm::zip_equal`.
`stablehlo.composite` accepts any number of regions, while the CHLO ops have a
fixed number, and nothing checked that the two agree. `zip_equal` only asserts
on equal lengths; without assertions it iterates over the composite's regions,
so a composite with more regions than the CHLO op made the pattern access
regions past the end of the new op, and one with fewer left the new op with an
empty region.

Compare the region counts before moving the regions and fail the match when
they differ, erasing the op that was just created so the IR is left unchanged.
Such a composite is then left in place, like any other composite that the
pass does not recompose.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019015280

display_title: Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

head_commit.message:
Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

`command_buffer_kernels.cc` previously embedded `.target sm_50` PTX strings for `set_case_condition`, `set_while_condition`, and `noop`. On the first conditional command buffer recording per device, `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` JIT-compiled that PTX on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` pool, stalling first recording by ~187 ms on `sm_103a` and serializing compilation across GPUs.

So this change compiles `set_case_condition`, `set_while_condition`, and `NoOp` as CUDA C++ kernels in `command_buffer_kernels.cu.cc` using `embeddable_cuda_library` (with `register_with_cudart = False` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary on drivers older than CUDA 12.3) and resolves their `KernelLoaderSpec`s via `FindCudaRuntimeKernel`. This returns in-memory CUBIN specs that `CudaExecutor::LoadKernel` loads directly via `LoadModuleFromCuBin` (`LoadCubin`), avoiding both the single-threaded PTX driver JIT and `cudaGetFuncBySymbol`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019895680

display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018968753

display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

display_title: Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

head_commit.message:
Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

`command_buffer_kernels.cc` previously embedded `.target sm_50` PTX strings for `set_case_condition`, `set_while_condition`, and `noop`. On the first conditional command buffer recording per device, `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` JIT-compiled that PTX on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` pool, stalling first recording by ~187 ms on `sm_103a` and serializing compilation across GPUs.

So this change compiles `set_case_condition`, `set_while_condition`, and `NoOp` as CUDA C++ kernels in `command_buffer_kernels.cu.cc` using `embeddable_cuda_library` (with `register_with_cudart = False` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary on drivers older than CUDA 12.3) and resolves their `KernelLoaderSpec`s via `FindCudaRuntimeKernel`. This returns in-memory CUBIN specs that `CudaExecutor::LoadKernel` loads directly via `LoadModuleFromCuBin` (`LoadCubin`), avoiding both the single-threaded PTX driver JIT and `cudaGetFuncBySymbol`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Scale Triton fusion warps up to 16 and 32 for large tiles.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Scale Triton fusion warps up to 16 and 32 for large tiles.

***Problem:*** `EstimateNumWarps` caps every Triton fusion at 8 warps regardless of register pressure, causing non-dot fusions with large live tiles, multiple wide reductions, or wide epilogue inputs alongside a reduction to drop to single-block SM residency or spill registers.

***Solution:*** Scale non-dot Triton fusions to 16 or 32 warps when live tile sizes, cumulative reduced elements, or independent wide epilogue inputs exceed single-block register thresholds, while keeping dot fusions capped at 8 warps and clamping to the target device's threads-per-block limit.

display_title: Support `register_with_cudart` in `embeddable_cuda_library` via `objcopy`

head_commit.message:
Support `register_with_cudart` in `embeddable_cuda_library` via `objcopy`

Replaces `-Wl,--wrap=__cudaRegister*` in `embeddable_cuda_library` and `cudart_kernel_registry` with an `objcopy --redefine-sym` rule (`_redefine_cuda_register_syms`) on the compiled object files, and adds a `register_with_cudart` attribute (defaulting to `True`).

When `register_with_cudart = True`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary` and `__cudaRegisterFunction` are renamed to `__xla_cudart_cudaRegister*`, which registers the fatbinary and kernel symbols in XLA's `KernelRegistry` and forwards to `libcudart`.

When `register_with_cudart = False`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary`, `__cudaRegisterFunction`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd`, and `__cudaUnregisterFatBinary` are renamed to `__xla_isolated_cudaRegister*`, registering the fatbinary and kernel symbols only in XLA's `KernelRegistry` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add tiling space and tile propagation for single-indexed gather

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add tiling space and tile propagation for single-indexed gather

`TilingSpace` now registers a runtime variable for the start index of a gather
with a single indexed dimension and no batching dimensions
(`TilingSpace::ProcessGather`), and `PropagateTileToInput` propagates a gather
output tile to its operands (`PropagateTileToInputForGatherOp`):
- `start_indices` gets the batch dimension tiles of the output (which must have
  size 1; their stride is normalized to 1) and a size-1 tile for
  `index_vector_dim`; this one-element tile defines the runtime variable.
- The gathered operand gets size-1 tiles on `collapsed_slice_dims`, the offset
  dimension tiles of the output on the other dimensions, and its indexed
  dimension is shifted by the runtime variable.
Unsupported gathers (several indexed dimensions, batching dimensions, sub-byte
types, unsigned index types, batch tiles larger than 1) return Unimplemented.

This is NFC for production: gather is still unsupported by the Triton support
checks, and every pass that tiles a fusion checks Triton support first (or only
sees fusions that are already Triton fusions); the CPU tiled emitter rejects
gather in `IsSupportedTiledFusion` before tiling.

display_title: Match StableSortExpander-expanded sort comparators in xla::TopkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
Match StableSortExpander-expanded sort comparators in xla::TopkRewriter.

When `StableSortExpander` runs before `TopkRewriter` (for example, in a
post-SPMD simplification pass), a stable TopK `kSort` has `is_stable=false`
and its comparator root is wrapped in `Select(Eq(old_root, cloned_root),
Lt(Parameter(2), Parameter(3)), old_root)`, where `cloned_root` computes the
same key comparison with swapped parameters `(1, 0)`. Extend `MatchNanSafeGt`
in `xla/service/topk_rewriter.cc` to verify both `old_root` and `cloned_root`
and preserve `is_stable = true` on the resulting `TopK` custom call in
`CreateTopKCustomCall`.

Replaces `-Wl,--wrap=__cudaRegister*` in `embeddable_cuda_library` and `cudart_kernel_registry` with an `objcopy --redefine-sym` rule (`_redefine_cuda_register_syms`) on the compiled object files, and adds a `register_with_cudart` attribute (defaulting to `True`).

When `register_with_cudart = True`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary` and `__cudaRegisterFunction` are renamed to `__xla_cudart_cudaRegister*`, which registers the fatbinary and kernel symbols in XLA's `KernelRegistry` and forwards to `libcudart`.

When `register_with_cudart = False`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary`, `__cudaRegisterFunction`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd`, and `__cudaUnregisterFatBinary` are renamed to `__xla_isolated_cudaRegister*`, registering the fatbinary and kernel symbols only in XLA's `KernelRegistry` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary.

display_title: Add `TraceMeFilter::kTraceHostEnqueueCallback = 1` and `TraceMeFilter::kTraceDefault = 2` in `trace_filter_utils.h`, and make `kTraceMeDefaultFilterMask` in `traceme.h` carry only the `kTraceDefault` bit (mask `0x4`) instead of every bit.

head_commit.message:
Add `TraceMeFilter::kTraceHostEnqueueCallback = 1` and `TraceMeFilter::kTraceDefault = 2` in `trace_filter_utils.h`, and make `kTraceMeDefaultFilterMask` in `traceme.h` carry only the `kTraceDefault` bit (mask `0x4`) instead of every bit.

TraceMe events that do not pass a filter mask now carry only the `kTraceDefault` bit, so a session with a filter mask records them only if its mask includes `kTraceDefault`. Every filter, including future ones, is therefore exclusive by default: a session with `host_traceme_filter_mask = (1ULL << kTraceHostEnqueueCallback)` records only events tagged with that bit. Sessions without a filter mask still record every event, and events tagged with `kTraceDefault` plus another bit are recorded both by those sessions and by sessions that filter on the other bit.

`traceme.h` cannot depend on `trace_filter_utils.h`, so it defines `kTraceMeHostEnqueueCallbackFilter` and `kTraceMeDefaultFilter` with the same values, and `traceme_recorder_test` checks with `static_assert`s that they stay equal. `traceme_recorder_test` covers sessions without a filter and with the `kTraceHostEnqueueCallback`, `kTraceMemory`, `kTraceMemory | kTraceDefault`, `kTraceDefault`, and an unused filter bit.

display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add tiling space and tile propagation for single-indexed gather

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add tiling space and tile propagation for single-indexed gather

`TilingSpace` now registers a runtime variable for the start index of a gather
with a single indexed dimension and no batching dimensions
(`TilingSpace::ProcessGather`), and `PropagateTileToInput` propagates a gather
output tile to its operands (`PropagateTileToInputForGatherOp`):
- `start_indices` gets the batch dimension tiles of the output (which must have
  size 1; their stride is normalized to 1) and a size-1 tile for
  `index_vector_dim`; this one-element tile defines the runtime variable.
- The gathered operand gets size-1 tiles on `collapsed_slice_dims`, the offset
  dimension tiles of the output on the other dimensions, and its indexed
  dimension is shifted by the runtime variable.
Unsupported gathers (several indexed dimensions, batching dimensions, sub-byte
types, unsigned index types, batch tiles larger than 1) return Unimplemented.

This is NFC for production: gather is still unsupported by the Triton support
checks, and every pass that tiles a fusion checks Triton support first (or only
sees fusions that are already Triton fusions); the CPU tiled emitter rejects
gather in `IsSupportedTiledFusion` before tiling.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Size F32 RAFT select_k scratch buffers dynamically.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Size F32 RAFT select_k scratch buffers dynamically.

`TopkSpecializer` previously allocated a hardcoded 32 MiB scratch buffer for every RAFT `__gpu$TopK` custom call, over-allocating on small TopK shapes (for example, 32 MiB instead of 4.5 KiB for `f32[8]`) while risking `FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource` exhaustion on large batch or vocabulary shapes.

Extract `choose_select_k_algorithm_float` into host-only `xla/backends/gpu/runtime/raft_select_k_utils` (shared with `select_k_exec_raft_float.cc`) alongside `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesFloat` and `GetRaftSelectKMaxSmCount`. The estimator bounds WarpSort and two-phase Radix workspace allocations across CUDA thread-block occupancy outcomes and full-die architecture SM ceilings (covering cross-SKU and MIG-to-full-GPU execution), and adds a `max(4 KiB, ~6.25%)` 256-byte-aligned safety margin.

Update `TopkSpecializer` to take `se::DeviceDescription` directly and size `F32` `__gpu$TopK` scratch buffers via `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesFloat` (`BF16` and `U64` remain on the 32 MiB fallback for follow-up changes). Use `RaftScratchPhaseMode::kSumAcrossPhases` during the 14-day GPU AOT forward-compatibility window, and regenerate `v2` GPU AOT compatibility goldens (`f32[8]` `k=1` preallocated scratch drops from 32.00 MiB to 4.5 KiB).

display_title: Match StableSortExpander-expanded sort comparators in xla::TopkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
Match StableSortExpander-expanded sort comparators in xla::TopkRewriter.

When `StableSortExpander` runs before `TopkRewriter` (for example, in a
post-SPMD simplification pass), a stable TopK `kSort` has `is_stable=false`
and its comparator root is wrapped in `Select(Eq(old_root, cloned_root),
Lt(Parameter(2), Parameter(3)), old_root)`, where `cloned_root` computes the
same key comparison with swapped parameters `(1, 0)`. Extend `MatchNanSafeGt`
in `xla/service/topk_rewriter.cc` to verify both `old_root` and `cloned_root`
and preserve `is_stable = true` on the resulting `TopK` custom call in
`CreateTopKCustomCall`.

Allow `HostMemoryAllocator` implementations to gracefully signal allocation
failures instead of crashing when host memory cannot be allocated.

`CommonPjRtClient`, and `TpuRawBuffer::CopyToViaBounceBuffer` to propagate
`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` errors when host buffer allocation fails.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Remove every operand slot of an instruction fused into a callable

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove every operand slot of an instruction fused into a callable

A callable instruction can hold the same producer in several operand slots, for example after rematerialization replaces operands one slot at a time. `CloneAndAppendInstructionIntoCalledComputation` replaced the parameter of the first matching slot, stopped, and detached the callable from the producer. The other slots still referenced the producer, but its user list no longer named the callable. The next user removal on that edge failed the check in `HloInstruction::Users::UserId`, and deleting the dead producer left a stale operand pointer.

The loop now removes every matching parameter and operand slot before detaching the callable. It walks the operands in reverse, because each removal shifts only higher indices. Callables without repeated operands behave as before, and no flag is added.

Tests:
- `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/hlo/ir:hlo_instruction_test`: pins `FuseInstruction` of a producer that occupies two adjacent operand slots.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019753843

display_title: [XLA] Fix heap-use-after-free when iterating computations in AllReduceReassociate

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix heap-use-after-free when iterating computations in AllReduceReassociate

AllReduceReassociate::RunImpl iterated lazily over
module->computations(execution_threads), which is a live view directly
over HloModule::computations_ (a std::vector<std::unique_ptr<HloComputation>>),
not a snapshot. When an all-reduce's to_apply computation must be promoted
to a wider type, RunImpl calls HloModule::AddEmbeddedComputation, which
push_backs onto computations_ and can reallocate it. That invalidates the
outer loop's iterator, so a subsequent ++/dereference reads freed memory.

Iterate over module->MakeNonfusionComputations(execution_threads) instead,
which is an explicit snapshot safe for concurrent mutation (per its own
doc comment in hlo_module.h), matching the pattern already used by
AssociativeScanRewriter::RunImpl and the recent ReduceWindowRewriter fix
for the same bug class (tensorflow/tensorflow@e80d3b46b7b, Fixes:
https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49822).

Added a regression test that generates 60 independent promotion events in
one module so HloModule::computations_ is certain to reallocate mid-loop.
Verified under ASan:

  AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free ... in operator*
    #4 xla::AllReduceReassociate::RunImpl(...)
       xla/hlo/transforms/collectives/all_reduce_reassociate.cc:182

freed by HloModule::AddEmbeddedComputation -> AddComputationInternal ->
vector::push_back, called from RunImpl's should_promote_ar path at
all_reduce_reassociate.cc:325. The test fails (ASan heap-use-after-free)
against the unpatched code and passes cleanly with this fix.

display_title: Match StableSortExpander-expanded sort comparators in xla::TopkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
Match StableSortExpander-expanded sort comparators in xla::TopkRewriter.

When `StableSortExpander` runs before `TopkRewriter` (for example, in a
post-SPMD simplification pass), a stable TopK `kSort` has `is_stable=false`
and its comparator root is wrapped in `Select(Eq(old_root, cloned_root),
Lt(Parameter(2), Parameter(3)), old_root)`, where `cloned_root` computes the
same key comparison with swapped parameters `(1, 0)`. Extend `MatchNanSafeGt`
in `xla/service/topk_rewriter.cc` to verify both `old_root` and `cloned_root`
and preserve `is_stable = true` on the resulting `TopK` custom call in
`CreateTopKCustomCall`.

display_title: Gracefully handle host memory allocation failures in PJRT.

head_commit.message:
Gracefully handle host memory allocation failures in PJRT.

Allow `HostMemoryAllocator` implementations to gracefully signal allocation
failures instead of crashing when host memory cannot be allocated.

Annotate `HostMemoryAllocator::Allocate` with `absl_nullable` to document that
it returns `nullptr` on allocation failure, and update `LinearizeThrottler`,
`CommonPjRtClient`, and `TpuRawBuffer::CopyToViaBounceBuffer` to propagate
`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` errors when host buffer allocation fails.

display_title: Clear incompatible tiled sharding on TopK custom calls in xla::TopkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
Clear incompatible tiled sharding on TopK custom calls in xla::TopkRewriter.

`CreateTopKCustomCall` creates the 2D `TopK` custom call and its
`get-tuple-element` outputs via `sort->AddInstruction(...)`, which calls
`SetupDerivedInstruction` and copies `sort`'s sharding whenever the tuple tree
structure matches (`ShapeUtil::CompatibleKind`). When `sort` has rank > 2 (so
its input is reshaped to 2D before `TopK` and reshaped back afterward) or is 2D
with `sort_dim == 0` (so its input is transposed before `TopK` and transposed
back afterward), a tiled sharding on `sort` has the wrong rank or transposed
tile dimensions for the 2D `TopK` custom call and its `get-tuple-element`
instructions. Clear tiled sharding on `topk`, `value_gte`, and `index_gte` in
those cases while preserving non-tiled shardings (such as `{manual}` or
`{replicated}`) and 1D/2D `sort_dim == 1` tiled shardings.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019731683

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify replicated product all-reduce for two participants

Replace a product all-reduce with a local square when the existing replication
analysis proves the input is replicated and every group has two participants.
Keep larger groups unchanged to avoid reassociating multiplications, and
preserve control dependencies and instruction metadata.

Add pass regressions for scalar and array inputs, replica subgroups, unsupported
cases, and control dependencies, plus a two-device execution comparison.

Fixes #51565.

display_title: Chunk sub-tile unpacking in tiled delinearizer.

head_commit.message:
Chunk sub-tile unpacking in tiled delinearizer.

Delinearizing sub-tile-packed tensors previously allocated an unpacked host buffer spanning the entire array before transposing into the output literal. Large packed arrays caused tens of gigabytes of unreserved host memory growth.

This change unpacks and transposes sub-tile-packed device-to-host data in bounded megabyte-scale chunks above the scratch threshold. Each chunk reuses small scratch storage and uses parallel transpose execution whenever the chunk plan exposes parallelism.

display_title: Avoid dereferencing end() in HloSharding::GetSubSharding.

head_commit.message:
Avoid dereferencing end() in HloSharding::GetSubSharding.

`HloSharding::GetSubSharding` constructed a subspan of `tuple_elements_` by
taking `&*begin_it` and `&*(begin_it + leaf_count)`. When the sub-tuple extends
to the end of `tuple_elements_` or is an empty tuple, this dereferences
`tuple_elements_.end()`, which is undefined behavior and traps under libc++
bounded iterators.

Slice `absl::MakeConstSpan(tuple_elements_).subspan(sharding_index, leaf_count)`
instead, after checking `sharding_index + leaf_count <= tuple_elements_.size()`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it for chunk-assigning heap algorithms, while keeping stats-only runs (`NoFragmentationStatsHeap` in `MinimumMemoryForModule`) restricted to direct operands so schedule scoring in `DefaultMemoryScheduler` does not change.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020624697

[TF/XLA] Finalize Bazel 8 Bzlmod cleanup and mark XLA extensions reproducible.

Clean up remaining Bazel 8 / Bzlmod migration items across TensorFlow and XLA:
* Pin `envoy_api` to `0.0.0-20260130-84e8436` in TensorFlow's `MODULE.bazel`
  (matching XLA) so `bazel mod show_repo --all_repos` resolves cleanly.
* Fix Windows `ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE` ("The filename or extension is too
  long") when loading `.pyd` extensions in the 251-259 char path range under
  Bzlmod (`rules_python`'s `_WindowsExtensionPathFinder` only added `\\?\` at
  `>= 260` chars, missing Win32 `LoadLibraryExW` `.manifest` probing) via
  `//third_party/py:rules_python_windows_long_path.patch`.
* Remove obsolete `--features=-external_include_paths` and
  `--host_features=-external_include_paths` from `.bazelrc` and XLA's
  `tensorflow.bazelrc` (now that `rules_cc` is `0.2.25 >= 0.2.22`), propagate
  `CompilationContext.external_includes` through `system_includes` in
  `xla/tsl/transitive_dependencies.bzl` (`_transitive_parameters_library_impl`,
  used by `custom_op_cc_header_only_library` such as
  `//tensorflow/core:framework_headers_lib`), and remove the duplicate
  `common:windows --features=compiler_param_file`.
* Mark deterministic XLA module extensions reproducible via
  `mctx.extension_metadata(reproducible = True)` (all 12 remaining extensions
  under `third_party/` and `build_tools/pjrt_wheels/`).
* Replace deprecated `$(location ...)` with `$(execpath ...)` in
  `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/BUILD`, bump `BAZEL_VERSION` to `8.8.2` in
  `tensorflow/tools/ci_build/install/install_bazel_from_source.sh`, and
  document the Bazel 8.8.2 / Bzlmod and C++/CUDA dependency upgrades in
  `RELEASE.md`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Clear incompatible tiled sharding on TopK custom calls in xla::TopkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
Clear incompatible tiled sharding on TopK custom calls in xla::TopkRewriter.

`CreateTopKCustomCall` creates the 2D `TopK` custom call, its
`get-tuple-element` outputs, and its input/output `reshape` and `transpose`
instructions via `sort->AddInstruction(...)`, which calls
`SetupDerivedInstruction` and copies `sort`'s sharding whenever the tuple tree
structure matches (`ShapeUtil::CompatibleKind`). When `sort` has rank > 2 (so
its input is reshaped to 2D before `TopK` and reshaped back afterward) or is 2D
with `sort_dim == 0` (so its input is transposed before `TopK` and transposed
back afterward), a tiled sharding on `sort` has the wrong rank or transposed
tile dimensions for the 2D `TopK` custom call, its `get-tuple-element`
instructions, and (for 1-operand sorts) the input/output `reshape` and
`transpose` instructions. Clear tiled sharding on `sort` before creating those
instructions while preserving non-tiled shardings (such as `{manual}` or
`{replicated}`) and 1D/2D `sort_dim == 1` tiled shardings.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019731683

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Add AVX-512 kernels for 4-bit PackIntN and UnpackIntN.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Add AVX-512 kernels for 4-bit PackIntN and UnpackIntN.

The generic `LoadInterleaved2` and `StoreInterleaved2` loops in `xla/packing.cc` expand to multi-step cross-lane byte shuffles and fall back to scalar loops for tails shorter than 128 elements, bottlenecking 4-bit tensor packing and unpacking on AVX-512 CPUs.

Add AVX-512 (`HWY_AVX3` and newer) paths to `Pack4Impl` and `Unpack4Impl`:

* `Pack4Impl` masks inputs to 4 bits, combines adjacent byte pairs via `SatWidenMulPairwiseAdd` (`vpmaddubsw` with `(1, 16)` multipliers), and narrows two vectors with `OrderedDemote2To` (`vpackuswb` + `vpermq`), with a single masked `vpmovwb` store path for inputs up to 64 elements. On `HWY_AVX3_DL` and `HWY_AVX3_SPR`, an empty inline-assembly barrier on the multiplier prevents LLVM from fusing `vpackuswb` + `vpermq` into `vpermt2b` (3 uops on Intel instead of 2, which slowed down 1024–10000 element calls by 8–14%), while `HWY_AVX3_ZEN4` retains the fused instruction.
* `Unpack4Impl` zero-extends 32 packed bytes to 16-bit lanes and computes `(wide | (wide << 4)) & 0x0F0F`.
* Both kernels handle sub-vector tails with AVX-512BW masked loads and stores and use a manual 4x unrolled loop followed by a `HWY_UNROLL(1)` 1x loop to avoid LLVM's runtime-unroll trip-count setup on small inputs (except `Unpack4Impl` on `HWY_AVX3`, where LLVM's default loop is 4.7% faster at 10000 elements).

Across 37 to 1048576 elements, this speeds up `PackIntN<4>` by 1.31× geomean on Sapphire Rapids / Emerald Rapids / Granite Rapids (1.30× on Emerald Rapids), 1.24× on Zen 4/5, and 1.40× on Skylake-SP / Cascade Lake, and speeds up `UnpackIntN<4>` by 1.25×, 1.18×, and 1.17× geomean respectively.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020557305

display_title: [TF/XLA] Finalize Bazel 8 Bzlmod cleanup and mark XLA extensions reproducible.

head_commit.message:
[TF/XLA] Finalize Bazel 8 Bzlmod cleanup and mark XLA extensions reproducible.

Clean up remaining Bazel 8 / Bzlmod migration items across TensorFlow and XLA:
* Pin `envoy_api` to `0.0.0-20260130-84e8436` in TensorFlow's `MODULE.bazel`
  (matching XLA) so `bazel mod show_repo --all_repos` resolves cleanly.
* Fix Windows `ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE` ("The filename or extension is too
  long") when loading `.pyd` extensions in the 251-259 char path range under
  Bzlmod (`rules_python`'s `_WindowsExtensionPathFinder` only added `\\?\` at
  `>= 260` chars, missing Win32 `LoadLibraryExW` `.manifest` probing) via
  `//third_party/py:rules_python_windows_long_path.patch`.
* Remove obsolete `--features=-external_include_paths` and
  `--host_features=-external_include_paths` from `.bazelrc` and XLA's
  `tensorflow.bazelrc` (now that `rules_cc` is `0.2.25 >= 0.2.22`), propagate
  `CompilationContext.external_includes` through `system_includes` in
  `xla/tsl/transitive_dependencies.bzl` (`_transitive_parameters_library_impl`,
  used by `custom_op_cc_header_only_library` such as
  `//tensorflow/core:framework_headers_lib`), and remove the duplicate
  `common:windows --features=compiler_param_file`.
* Mark deterministic XLA module extensions reproducible via
  `mctx.extension_metadata(reproducible = True)` (all 12 remaining extensions
  under `third_party/` and `build_tools/pjrt_wheels/`).
* Replace deprecated `$(location ...)` with `$(execpath ...)` in
  `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/BUILD`, bump `BAZEL_VERSION` to `8.8.2` in
  `tensorflow/tools/ci_build/install/install_bazel_from_source.sh`, and
  document the Bazel 8.8.2 / Bzlmod and C++/CUDA dependency upgrades in
  `RELEASE.md`.

display_title: Fix TF loop event grouping with ThreadpoolListener::Region.

head_commit.message:
Fix TF loop event grouping with ThreadpoolListener::Region.

When a TensorFlow `while_loop` runs in the executor, `NextIteration` in iteration `k` can activate `Merge` for iteration `k + 1` inline on the same worker thread inside a single `ThreadpoolListener::Region` closure (or schedule tasks for iteration `k + 1` before `iteration_scope` updates). Enabling consumer context stats on `ThreadpoolListener::Region` previously caused iteration `k`'s group propagation to overwrite subsequent loop iterations into a single step group, and left duplicate consumer stats on paired `ThreadpoolListener::StartRegion` markers.

- Track active regions with a stack in `ThreadpoolLineMutator::MutateEventsInLine` (supporting zero-timestamp starts, nested inline closures, and `uint64_t` region IDs), copy `ContextType::kThreadpoolEvent` consumer stats onto `ThreadpoolListener::Region`, and strip consumer stats from paired `StartRegion` markers so `AddFlowsToXplane` emits a single `kFlowIn` endpoint per region.
- Pre-assign `group_id` to all entry `ExecutorState::Process` events of each TensorFlow loop iteration in `EventForest::ProcessTensorFlowLoop`, and update `EventNode::PropagateGroupId` so BFS expands nodes matching `group_id` while stopping at nodes pre-assigned to other groups.
- Skip intra-thread parent edges onto `ProcessBatch` and `OrbaxServing::ProcessBatch` in `EventForest::ConnectIntraThread` so chained batch scheduler closures do not merge distinct batches across `ThreadpoolListener::Region`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015690057

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

### Status quo

In the XLA:CPU MLIR fusion pipeline, `f32` `log` uses a handwritten LLVM IR polynomial (`GenerateVF32Log`, 1.19 ULP max error), `f64` `log` falls back to scalar `libm` `log` calls (0.5 ULP, unvectorized), and `log1p` lowers to an algebraic composition around `log` (up to ~3.0 ULP in `f32`).

### Why

Compiling YNNPACK's `log` and `log1p` SIMD kernels (`f32` and `f64`, up to 512-bit vectors) to LLVM bitcode and inlining them during codegen vectorizes `f64` `log` and `log1p`, speeds up `f32` `log` and `log1p` across x86 and ARM64, improves `f32` accuracy (`log` 1.19 -> 1.02 ULP, `log1p` 3.0 -> 1.65 ULP), and deletes XLA:CPU's handwritten `GenerateVF32Log` C++ IR builder.

End-to-end `elementwise_benchmark_test` (`N = 128, 1024, 8192` geomean cycles/op vs baseline):
- `f32` (`BM_LogF32`, `BM_Log1pF32`): `-19.1%` on x86 AVX2+FMA3, `-28.8%` on x86 AVX-512, `-36.6%` on ARM64 NEON.
- `f64` (`BM_LogF64`, `BM_Log1pF64`): `1.7x-4.4x` faster across AVX2, AVX-512, and ARM64 NEON.

### Design choices

- Expose YNNPACK `log` and `log1p` wrappers for `f32` and `f64` vector widths up to 512 bits in `xla/codegen/intrinsic/cpp/ynnpack_unary.{h,cc}`, compile a single `ynnpack_unary_ll` bitcode library, inline from it during codegen, and stop splitting `v16f32` `log` on AVX-512.
- Keep upcasting `f16` and `bf16` to `f32`, since YNNPACK has no native full-precision 16-bit `log`/`log1p` kernels on x86.
- Preserve `log1p(-0.0) = -0.0` via `copysign`, and keep the existing `libm` and algebraic `Log1p` lowerings on GPU and when CppGen bitcode is unavailable.

### Compromises

Maximum error bounds in ULPs (from JAX's numerics test suite and `docs/accuracy.md`):

| Op | CPU (before) | CPU (this CL) | NVIDIA GPU | TPU (v6e / 7x) |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `log` (`f32`) | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.0 | 2.5 |
| `log` (`f64`) | 0.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log1p` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 1.0 | 3.0 |
| `log1p` (`f64`) | 2.0 | 2.0 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log10` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.5 | 2.5 | 3.0 |
| `logit` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 3.0 | 4.0 / 4.5 |
| `acosh` (`f32`) | 4.5 | 3.5 | 2.5 | 4.5 / 5.0 |
| `asinh` (`f32`) | 3.5 | 2.0 | 2.0 | 3.5 |
| `atanh` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 3.5 | 3.5 |

`f64` `log` trades scalar `libm`'s 0.5 ULP correct rounding for SIMD vectorization, matching GPU's 1.5 ULP bound (measured 1.23 ULP).

The `c128` `Log` exhaustive test gets a 1 ULP relative bound on CPU for inputs with tiny imaginary parts. CPU already flushes those imaginary parts to zero, which fails the distance check, so the real part `log|z|` was effectively held to exact `libm` results.

### Alternatives

- Tested a pure degree-8 Estrin polynomial (`Q = 1`) for `f32` `log` in YNNPACK, which avoided `fdiv` latency in isolation on wide AVX-512 vectors, but ran slower in XLA's unrolled elementwise loops across AVX2, AVX-512, and ARM64 NEON than the `[3/2]` rational kernel.
- Reaching `<= 1.0` ULP for both `log` and `log1p` requires split `ln(2)` plus double-word addition for `1 + x`, which added 18-68% per-vector overhead in microbenchmarks for accuracy tighter than GPU (`f64`) and TPU (`f32`).

### Updating tests

CPU `log` and `log1p` results move by about 1 ULP on many inputs, and by more in code that amplifies small differences (iterative solves, log-dets, KL divergences, derivatives). Tests that check exact equality, use tolerances below 1 ULP, or compare against goldens captured from the old output may fail. Please update them to allow a few ULP, or set goldens to exact reference values, rather than pinning bit-exact results.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020506814

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA][HLO Value Tracking] Propagate OriginalValue in TupleUtil.

head_commit.message:
[XLA][HLO Value Tracking] Propagate OriginalValue in TupleUtil.

`TupleUtil::ExtractPrefix`, `AppendSuffix`, `Duplicate`, `ReplaceTupleWith`, and `AddGetTupleElements` create `tuple`, `get-tuple-element`, and `bitcast` instructions without an `OriginalValue`, so every caller that wants to preserve HLO value tracking has to patch the original values up by hand after each call. Callers that don't (e.g. for the intermediate instructions `ReplaceTupleWith` creates for nested tuples) silently lose value tracking.

Since every element these helpers create holds the same value as the element it is taken from, derive the `OriginalValue`s of the created instructions from those of their inputs. An input's `OriginalValue` is only used if it matches the input's shape; inputs whose shape was changed in place without updating their `OriginalValue` leave the derived instructions without one, as before, instead of risking a crash or a misattributed value. Callers that widen shapes in place are responsible for keeping the `OriginalValue` in sync, which the new `AppendEmptyElementsToOriginalValue` helper does for the common case of appending tuple elements.

Update the callers accordingly:

* `WhileUtil::MakeInstructionsLiveIn` no longer copies `OriginalValue`s onto the results of `AppendSuffix` and `ExtractPrefix`.
* `HloControlFlowFlattening` and `WhileLoopIterationCap` keep the `OriginalValue`s of the instructions they widen in place in sync before building tuples from them, which also replaces the `AppendToWhileLoopOriginalValue` call in `WhileLoopIterationCap`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Size F32 RAFT select_k scratch buffers dynamically.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Size F32 RAFT select_k scratch buffers dynamically.

`TopkSpecializer` previously allocated a hardcoded 32 MiB scratch buffer for every RAFT `__gpu$TopK` custom call, over-allocating on small TopK shapes (for example, 32 MiB instead of 4.5 KiB for `f32[8]`) while risking `FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource` exhaustion on large batch or vocabulary shapes.

Extract `choose_select_k_algorithm_float` into host-only `xla/backends/gpu/runtime/raft_select_k_utils` (shared with `select_k_exec_raft_float.cc`) alongside `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesFloat` and `GetRaftSelectKMaxSmCount`. The estimator bounds WarpSort and two-phase Radix workspace allocations across CUDA thread-block occupancy outcomes and full-die architecture SM ceilings (covering cross-SKU and MIG-to-full-GPU execution), and adds a `max(4 KiB, ~6.25%)` 256-byte-aligned safety margin.

Update `TopkSpecializer` to take `se::DeviceDescription` directly and size `F32` `__gpu$TopK` scratch buffers via `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesFloat` (`BF16` and `U64` remain on the 32 MiB fallback for follow-up changes). Use `RaftScratchPhaseMode::kSumAcrossPhases` during the 14-day GPU AOT forward-compatibility window, and regenerate `v2` GPU AOT compatibility goldens (`f32[8]` `k=1` preallocated scratch drops from 32.00 MiB to 4.5 KiB).

display_title: [TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

head_commit.message:
[TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

Replace the `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` `single_version_override` and the
custom `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` attribute with a self-contained Starlark
repository rule (`local_wheel_repo` / `@local_tf_wheel`). Under Bzlmod,
`single_version_override` is ignored for non-root modules, so downstream
projects depending on TensorFlow via `MODULE.bazel` saw unpatched `rules_python`
and failed with `unknown attribute local_wheels provided`.

* Delete `third_party/py/rules_python_local_wheel.patch` and remove it along
  with `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` from `MODULE.bazel`.
* Add `third_party/extensions/local_wheel.bzl` (`local_wheel_repo`), a lazy,
  non-reproducible repository rule exposing `dist/<WHEEL_NAME>-*.whl` as
  `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` (watches `dist/` for incremental rebuilds, supports
  hyphen/underscore `WHEEL_NAME` variants, and safely produces an empty
  `filegroup` when `dist/` is absent).
* Update `tf_wheel_dep()` in `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/utils/tf_wheel.bzl`
  to return `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` under Bzlmod while keeping
  `@pypi//<WHEEL_NAME>:whl` under `--config=workspace`.

display_title: Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

head_commit.message:
Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

Previously, the MLIR-generated GPU `Pow` kernel lowered `stablehlo.power` to a Linalg/SCF exponentiation-by-squaring loop with a hardcoded upper bound of 6 iterations, which only inspected the lowest 6 bits of the exponent (`y % 64`) and discarded bits at positions >= 6. In addition, MHLO's `PowOp` scalar lowering used a fixed 6-iteration loop bound and a special-case even-base `select` that forced even bases with exponents >= 64 to 0. As a result, odd bases with exponents >= 64 (such as `(-47)**66`) and even bases with exponents >= 64 produced inconsistent results compared to CPU and NumPy fixed-width two's-complement wrap-around semantics.

Update the integer `Pow` lowering across `kernel_gen` and MHLO:
- In `LegalizeTensorReshapePass`, add a post-lowering rewrite (`FixIntegerPowLoopUpperBound`) that updates the `scf.for` loop upper bound emitted by `StablehloLegalizeToLinalgPass` from 6 to the integer element bit-width.
- In MHLO (`map_mhlo_to_scalar_op.h`), iterate up to the integer element bit-width and remove the special-case even-base select so both odd and even bases wrap consistently across all bit-widths.

Fixes #118202

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

### Status quo

In the XLA:CPU MLIR fusion pipeline, `f32` `log` uses a handwritten LLVM IR polynomial (`GenerateVF32Log`, 1.19 ULP max error), `f64` `log` falls back to scalar `libm` `log` calls (0.5 ULP, unvectorized), and `log1p` lowers to an algebraic composition around `log` (up to ~3.0 ULP in `f32`).

### Why

Compiling YNNPACK's `log` and `log1p` SIMD kernels (`f32` and `f64`, up to 512-bit vectors) to LLVM bitcode and inlining them during codegen vectorizes `f64` `log` and `log1p`, speeds up `f32` `log` and `log1p` across x86 and ARM64, improves `f32` accuracy (`log` 1.19 -> 1.02 ULP, `log1p` 3.0 -> 1.65 ULP), and deletes XLA:CPU's handwritten `GenerateVF32Log` C++ IR builder.

End-to-end `elementwise_benchmark_test` (`N = 128, 1024, 8192` geomean cycles/op vs baseline):
- `f32` (`BM_LogF32`, `BM_Log1pF32`): `-19.1%` on x86 AVX2+FMA3, `-28.8%` on x86 AVX-512, `-36.6%` on ARM64 NEON.
- `f64` (`BM_LogF64`, `BM_Log1pF64`): `1.7x-4.4x` faster across AVX2, AVX-512, and ARM64 NEON.

### Design choices

- Expose YNNPACK `log` and `log1p` wrappers for `f32` and `f64` vector widths up to 512 bits in `xla/codegen/intrinsic/cpp/ynnpack_unary.{h,cc}`, compile a single `ynnpack_unary_ll` bitcode library, inline from it during codegen, and stop splitting `v16f32` `log` on AVX-512.
- Keep upcasting `f16` and `bf16` to `f32`, since YNNPACK has no native full-precision 16-bit `log`/`log1p` kernels on x86.
- Preserve `log1p(-0.0) = -0.0` via `copysign`, and keep the existing `libm` and algebraic `Log1p` lowerings on GPU and when CppGen bitcode is unavailable.

### Compromises

Maximum error bounds in ULPs (from JAX's numerics test suite and `docs/accuracy.md`):

| Op | CPU (before) | CPU (this CL) | NVIDIA GPU | TPU (v6e / 7x) |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `log` (`f32`) | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.0 | 2.5 |
| `log` (`f64`) | 0.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log1p` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 1.0 | 3.0 |
| `log1p` (`f64`) | 2.0 | 2.0 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log10` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.5 | 2.5 | 3.0 |
| `logit` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 3.0 | 4.0 / 4.5 |
| `acosh` (`f32`) | 4.5 | 3.5 | 2.5 | 4.5 / 5.0 |
| `asinh` (`f32`) | 3.5 | 2.0 | 2.0 | 3.5 |
| `atanh` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 3.5 | 3.5 |

`f64` `log` trades scalar `libm`'s 0.5 ULP correct rounding for SIMD vectorization, matching GPU's 1.5 ULP bound (measured 1.23 ULP).

The `c128` `Log` exhaustive test gets a 1 ULP relative bound on CPU for inputs with tiny imaginary parts. CPU already flushes those imaginary parts to zero, which fails the distance check, so the real part `log|z|` was effectively held to exact `libm` results.

### Alternatives

- Tested a pure degree-8 Estrin polynomial (`Q = 1`) for `f32` `log` in YNNPACK, which avoided `fdiv` latency in isolation on wide AVX-512 vectors, but ran slower in XLA's unrolled elementwise loops across AVX2, AVX-512, and ARM64 NEON than the `[3/2]` rational kernel.
- Reaching `<= 1.0` ULP for both `log` and `log1p` requires split `ln(2)` plus double-word addition for `1 + x`, which added 18-68% per-vector overhead in microbenchmarks for accuracy tighter than GPU (`f64`) and TPU (`f32`).

### Updating tests

CPU `log` and `log1p` results move by about 1 ULP on many inputs, and by more in code that amplifies small differences (iterative solves, log-dets, KL divergences, derivatives). Tests that check exact equality, use tolerances below 1 ULP, or compare against goldens captured from the old output may fail. Please update them to allow a few ULP, or set goldens to exact reference values, rather than pinning bit-exact results.

display_title: [TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

head_commit.message:
[TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

Replace the `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` `single_version_override` and the
custom `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` attribute with a self-contained Starlark
repository rule (`local_wheel_repo` / `@local_tf_wheel`). Under Bzlmod,
`single_version_override` is ignored for non-root modules, so downstream
projects depending on TensorFlow via `MODULE.bazel` saw unpatched `rules_python`
and failed with `unknown attribute local_wheels provided`.

* Delete `third_party/py/rules_python_local_wheel.patch` and remove it along
  with `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` from `MODULE.bazel`.
* Add `third_party/extensions/local_wheel.bzl` (`local_wheel_repo`), a lazy,
  non-reproducible repository rule exposing `dist/<WHEEL_NAME>-*.whl` as
  `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` (watches `dist/` for incremental rebuilds, supports
  hyphen/underscore `WHEEL_NAME` variants, and safely produces an empty
  `filegroup` when `dist/` is absent).
* Update `tf_wheel_dep()` in `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/utils/tf_wheel.bzl`
  to return `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` under Bzlmod while keeping
  `@pypi//<WHEEL_NAME>:whl` under `--config=workspace`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019606401

display_title: [XLA] Add non pageable temporary buffer region option to BufferAssigner

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add non pageable temporary buffer region option to BufferAssigner

Some temporary buffers are addressed by an external agent at a fixed offset and
cannot be split into or moved across pages under multi page buffer assignment.
Add `BufferAssigner::Options::must_be_non_pageable` and
`BufferAllocation::is_non_pageable()` (persisted in `BufferAllocationProto`) so
callers can pack those buffers in a dedicated unpaged temporary allocation
across disjoint lifetimes. Covered by `buffer_assignment_test`.
